overall.assessment: Prema opisu tematskih blokova, podcast cjelovito povezuje zaštitu nerođenog života s priznanjem rane koju pobačaj može ostaviti i s pozivom na milosrđe, obraćenje i obnovu odnosa s Bogom. Svjedočanstvo o očevu sudjelovanju, molitvenom služenju i očinstvu promiče odgovornost muškaraca te kulturu susreta umjesto šutnje, osude ili napuštanja ranjenih osoba. Naglasak na oprostu i nadi dobro odgovara kršćanskom shvaćanju da se težina moralnog zla ne smije umanjivati, ali se čovjeka ne smije svesti na njegov grijeh niti mu uskratiti mogućnost obraćenja. Budući da je procjena utemeljena na sažetku tema, a ne na punom transkriptu, ostaje otvoreno koliko podcast izričito razjašnjava sakramentalnu narav pomirenja i razliku između duhovnog iscjeljenja i stručne pomoći kod depresije.
seeds_of_logos: Zaštita nerođenog djeteta kao osobe čije je dostojanstvo prisutno od začeća, uz razumijevanje da je pobačaj moralno teško zlo, a ne neutralan događaj.
Priznavanje da posljedice pobačaja mogu raniti i muškarce te da očinska odgovornost uključuje prisutnost, a ne pritisak ili napuštanje žene suočene s kriznom trudnoćom.
Svjedočanstvo, molitva i zajednica mogu pomoći osobama da iziđu iz izolacije i ponovno otkriju nadu; pristup ranjenima kao osobama koje trebaju pratnju odgovara slici milosrdnog Samarijanca.
Povezivanje služenja nerođenima s osobnim obraćenjem, oprostom i svakodnevnim obiteljskim životom, umjesto s pukim aktivizmom ili predstavljanjem vlastite svetosti.
Naglasak na muškoj molitvi, odgovornom očinstvu, zahvalnosti i obiteljskoj molitvi promiče obitelj kao zajednicu ljubavi i mjesto služenja životu.
Poruka da čovjek nakon teške prošlosti nije beznadno izgubljen može poduprijeti reintegrirajuće milosrđe: istinito priznanje zla uz poziv na pokajanje, oprost i novi život.
concerns: Formulacija poput „oprostio sam si” može biti duhovno korisna kao opis prihvaćanja Božjeg oprosta, ali bi bila nejasna ako se shvati kao samostalno oslobođenje od krivnje bez pokajanja, obraćenja i sakramentalnog pomirenja. Sažetak ne pokazuje kako je ta razlika u podcastu objašnjena.

Govori o čudesnom prijelazu iz depresije u radost i o duhovnom boju mogu biti snažna osobna svjedočanstva, ali ne bi ih trebalo prikazivati kao zajamčen ishod molitve niti kao zamjenu za stručnu psihološku ili zdravstvenu pomoć; dostupni sažetak ne omogućuje procjenu je li takva ograda izrečena.

Potrebno je istodobno jasno čuvati dostojanstvo nerođenog djeteta i suosjećajno razlikovati osobnu odgovornost pojedinaca prema njihovim okolnostima. Crkveno učenje osuđuje pobačaj, ali također prepoznaje da pritisci i teške okolnosti mogu utjecati na osobnu krivnju te traži pomoć i milosrđe, ne stigmatizaciju.
overall.theological_context: Evangelium vitae utemeljuje obranu nerođenog života na njegovu dostojanstvu pred Bogom i istodobno naglašava odgovornost očeva, obitelji, zdravstvenih djelatnika i društva; Dignitas infinita potvrđuje da dostojanstvo svakog čovjeka vrijedi od začeća do prirodne smrti. Benedikt XVI. opisuje odgovor Crkve ranjenima slikom milosrdnog Samarijanca: istina o ozbiljnosti pobačaja ne isključuje milosrdnu pratnju onih koji traže mir i mogućnost novog početka. U socijalnom nauku ta obrana života uključuje i konkretnu solidarnost s trudnicama i obiteljima u teškoćama, jer poštovanje života i briga za ranjive pripadaju zajedničkom dobru, a ne samo privatnoj pobožnosti.

citations.document_title: Abortion Shame, Abortion Shaming, and the Reintegrative Mercy of God (Evangelium Vitae §99)

overall.assessment_en: According to the description of the thematic blocks, the podcast comprehensively connects the protection of unborn life with the acknowledgment of the wound that abortion can leave and with a call to mercy, conversion, and the renewal of one's relationship with God. The testimony about a father's participation, prayer ministry, and fatherhood promotes the responsibility of men and a culture of encounter instead of silence, condemnation, or the abandonment of wounded persons. The emphasis on forgiveness and hope corresponds well to the Christian understanding that the gravity of moral evil must not be diminished, but man must not be reduced to his sin nor denied the possibility of conversion. Since the assessment is based on a summary of topics and not on a full transcript, it remains an open question to what extent the podcast explicitly clarifies the sacramental nature of reconciliation and the distinction between spiritual healing and professional help for depression.
overall.theological_context_en: Evangelium vitae grounds the defense of unborn life on its dignity before God and at the same time emphasizes the responsibility of fathers, families, healthcare workers, and society; Dignitas infinita confirms that the dignity of every human being is valid from conception to natural death. Benedict XVI describes the Church's response to the wounded with the image of the Good Samaritan: the truth about the gravity of abortion does not exclude the merciful accompaniment of those who seek peace and the possibility of a new beginning. In social teaching, this defense of life also includes concrete solidarity with pregnant women and families in difficulties, because respect for life and care for the vulnerable belong to the common good, not merely to private piety.
seeds_of_logos_en: The protection of the unborn child as a person whose dignity is present from conception, along with the understanding that abortion is a grave moral evil, and not a neutral event.

The recognition that the consequences of abortion can also wound men, and that fatherly responsibility includes presence, rather than pressure or the abandonment of a woman faced with a crisis pregnancy.
Testimony, prayer, and community can help persons emerge from isolation and rediscover hope; approaching the wounded as persons who need accompaniment corresponds to the image of the Good Samaritan.
Connecting ministry to the unborn with personal conversion, forgiveness, and daily family life, instead of with mere activism or presenting one's own holiness.
The emphasis on men's prayer, responsible fatherhood, gratitude, and family prayer promotes the family as a community of love and a place of service to life.

The message that a person is not hopelessly lost after a difficult past can support reintegrating mercy: the truthful acknowledgment of evil accompanied by a call to repentance, forgiveness, and new life.
concerns_en: A formulation like "I forgave myself" can be spiritually useful as a description of accepting God's forgiveness, but it would be unclear if understood as autonomous liberation from guilt without repentance, conversion, and sacramental reconciliation. The summary does not show how this distinction was explained in the podcast.

Talk of a miraculous transition from depression to joy and of spiritual warfare can be powerful personal testimonies, but they should not be presented as a guaranteed outcome of prayer nor as a substitute for professional psychological or medical help; the available summary does not allow for an assessment of whether such a caveat was expressed.

It is necessary at the same time to clearly uphold the dignity of the unborn child and compassionately distinguish the personal responsibility of individuals according to their circumstances. Church teaching condemns abortion, but also recognizes that pressures and difficult circumstances can affect personal guilt, and calls for help and mercy, not stigmatization.

sections.subtitle: Gost koji je voditelja „napokon oženio“
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj predstavlja gosta Vedrana Politea na početku epizode podcasta „Redefinicija“
sections.content:
Nova epizoda podcasta **„Redefinicija“** s kanala *Muževni budite* otvara se pozdravom „Hvaljen Isus i Marija, i sveti Josip“. Voditelj odmah predstavlja gosta: **Vedrana Politea**, dugogodišnjeg člana inicijative **„40 dana za život“** i provoditelja programa **„Iscjeljenje očeva srca“**. Dodaje i osobnu napomenu da je Politeo „jedan od glavnih razloga“ zašto se on sam napokon oženio. Tu priču ostavlja za kasnije u razgovoru.

Gost zahvaljuje na pozivu i kaže da mu je drago što je u studiju. Voditelj najavljuje da će razgovarati o inicijativi i o programu, ali početak želi posvetiti nečemu osobnijem. Obojica su, kako ističe, **obraćenici**, pa ga zanima kako je izgledao Politeov život prije obraćenja, a kako nakon njega.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim okvirom: navodi katolički pozdrav i predstavlja teme obraćenja, služenja nerođenima te pomoći nakon iskustva pobačaja, bez iznošenja spornih teoloških tvrdnji. Budući da je riječ samo o najavi razgovora, ne može se na temelju njega procijeniti nauk ili praksa programa „Iscjeljenje očeva srca“.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička pastoralna skrb nakon pobačaja povezuje istinito priznanje moralne težine čina s nadom u Božje milosrđe, oproštenje i mir u sakramentu pomirenja; Crkva također prepoznaje potrebu za duhovnom i psihološkom potporom. Kršćansko obraćenje stoga nije samo promjena životnog smjera nego i povratak Bogu, koji poziva na pokajanje i obnovu; ovaj uvodni odlomak najavljuje tu temu, ali još ne govori kako je gost razumije ili živi.

magisterium.assessment_en: The excerpt is largely aligned with the Catholic framework: it cites a Catholic greeting and introduces the topics of conversion, ministry to the unborn, and help after the experience of abortion, without putting forward contentious theological claims. Since it is only an announcement of the conversation, the teaching or practice of the program "Iscjeljenje očeva srca" cannot be evaluated on the basis of it.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic pastoral care after abortion connects the truthful acknowledgment of the moral gravity of the act with hope in God's mercy, forgiveness, and peace in the sacrament of reconciliation; the Church also recognizes the need for spiritual and psychological support. Christian conversion is therefore not only a change of life direction but also a return to God, who calls to repentance and renewal; this introductory excerpt announces that theme, but does not yet speak of how the guest understands or lives it.

sections.subtitle_en: The guest who "finally got the host married"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host introduces the guest Vedran Politeo at the beginning of the episode of the podcast "Redefinicija"
sections.content_en:
A new episode of the podcast **"Redefinicija"** from the channel *Muževni budite* opens with the greeting "Praise be Jesus and Mary, and Saint Joseph". The host immediately introduces the guest: **Vedran Politeo**, a longtime member of the initiative **"40 dana za život"** and implementer of the program **"Iscjeljenje očeva srca"**. He also adds a personal note that Politeo is "one of the main reasons" why he himself finally got married. He leaves that story for later in the conversation.

The guest thanks him for the invitation and says that he is glad to be in the studio. The host announces that they will talk about the initiative and about the program, but wants to dedicate the beginning to something more personal. Both are, as he points out, **converts**, so he is interested in what Politeo's life looked like before conversion, and what it looked like after it.

sections.subtitle: „Ti postojiš, ali nemoj ulaziti u moj život“
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Politeo opisuje svoj površan odnos s Isusom u djetinjstvu
sections.content:
Vedran Politeo rođen je u obitelji koja je slavila Uskrs i Božić, ali u kojoj nitko nije bio praktični vjernik. Kad danas razmišlja o tom razdoblju, primjećuje da je u njemu postojala želja da upozna Isusa i da je vjerovao kako je On živ. Odnos koji je tada imao s Bogom opisuje ovako: „Okej, Ti postojiš, Ti si tu, ali nemoj ulaziti u moj život. Ja se neću Tebe dirati, neću biti kao svi ostali ljudi da Te nešto žicaju stalno.“ Isus mu je, kaže, bio poput prijatelja koji ide uz njega, dok je svatko išao svojim putem. Tako je bilo dugo, a vjera se pritom nije produbljivala.

Zanimanje za vjeru javilo se krajem osnovne, odnosno u srednjoj školi. Prijatelj kojemu je Politeo kasnije bio vjenčani kum primio je sve sakramente i pohađao vjeronauk za one koji su ih već primili. Pitao je svećenika može li dovesti nekoga, pa se Politeo, tada samo kršten, priključio skupini. Vjeronauk je vodio **Mijo Gorski**, današnji biskup. Politeo ga pamti kao čovjeka koji je lijepo radio s mladima i dopuštao različita razmišljanja i slobodnu komunikaciju kako bi im približio Isusa. Taj je vjeronauk pohađao oko godinu dana.

Unatoč tome, odlučio je ne primiti sakramente. Bile su to 90-e, nakon raspada Jugoslavije i stvaranja Hrvatske, kada su mnogi pristupali sakramentima, a voditelj dodaje: „Postali katolici.“ Politeo danas kaže da ga je tada „đavo lijepo zaveo“ mišlju „ne budi k'o svi“, jer je uvijek želio biti poseban i drugačiji.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim razumijevanjem vjere kao osobnog odnosa s Isusom koji treba sazrijevati i zahvatiti život, a ne ostati na običaju ili nejasnom osjećaju. Politeova želja da Boga drži izvan svakodnevnog života i odluka da ne primi sakramente prikazane su kao osobno udaljavanje od vjere, ne kao nešto što se preporučuje.
concerns: Izraz „Postali katolici“ može biti neprecizan ako se odnosi na ljude koji su već bili katolici, a tada su samo primili sakramente ili obnovili vjerski život; sam odlomak ne daje dovoljno podataka da bi se utvrdilo na koga se točno odnosi.

Tvrdnja da ga je „đavo lijepo zaveo“ može se razumjeti kao osobno, retrospektivno prepoznavanje duhovne napasti. Ipak, bilo bi teološki jednostrano svesti odluku samo na đavolsku obmanu, bez priznavanja čovjekove slobode i osobne odgovornosti.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko shvaćanje vjere uključuje osobno prianjanje uz Boga i slobodan pristanak na objavljenu istinu; zrelo vjerovanje zato nije samo sjećanje na vjeronauk ili osjećaj da je Isus blizu. Sakramenti nisu tek društveni običaj, nego dar Božje milosti koji traži odgovor vjere i uvodi u trajan hod s Kristom. Odlomak dobro prenosi razliku između početnog osjećaja Isusove blizine i dubljeg učeništva, premda njegov opis osobnog iskustva sam po sebi ne predstavlja cjelovit nauk o sakramentima ili duhovnoj borbi.
magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with the Catholic understanding of faith as a personal relationship with Jesus that should mature and take hold of life, rather than remain at custom or a vague feeling. Politeo's desire to keep God out of everyday life and his decision not to receive the sacraments are presented as a personal distancing from faith, not as something that is recommended.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of faith includes personal adherence to God and free assent to revealed truth; mature belief is therefore not merely a memory of religious education or a feeling that Jesus is near. The sacraments are not merely a social custom, but a gift of God's grace that calls for a response of faith and introduces one into an enduring walk with Christ. The passage conveys well the difference between an initial feeling of Jesus' nearness and deeper discipleship, although its description of personal experience does not in itself represent a complete teaching on the sacraments or spiritual combat.
concerns_en: The phrase "Became Catholics" may be imprecise if it refers to people who were already Catholics, and at that time only received the sacraments or renewed their religious life; the passage itself does not provide enough data to determine exactly whom it refers to.

The claim that "the devil nicely seduced him" can be understood as a personal, retrospective recognition of spiritual temptation. Still, it would be theologically one-sided to reduce the decision merely to demonic deception, without acknowledging human freedom and personal responsibility.

sections.subtitle_en: "You exist, but don't enter into my life"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Politeo describes his superficial relationship with Jesus in childhood
sections.content_en:
Vedran Politeo was born into a family that celebrated Easter and Christmas, but in which no one was a practicing believer. When he reflects on that period today, he notices that there was a desire within him to get to know Jesus and that he believed that He was alive. The relationship he had with God back then he describes like this: "Okay, You exist, You are here, but don't enter into my life. I won't touch You, I won't be like all the other people begging You for something all the time." Jesus was, he says, like a friend to him who walked alongside him, while each went their own way. It was like that for a long time, and faith did not deepen in the process.

Interest in faith arose at the end of elementary school, that is, in high school. A friend for whom Politeo was later the best man received all the sacraments and attended religious education for those who had already received them. He asked the priest if he could bring someone along, so Politeo, at that time only baptized, joined the group. The religious education was led by **Mijo Gorski**, today's bishop. Politeo remembers him as a man who worked well with young people and allowed diverse thinking and open communication in order to bring Jesus closer to them. He attended that religious education for about a year.

Despite that, he decided not to receive the sacraments. Those were the '90s, after the collapse of Yugoslavia and the creation of Croatia, when many approached the sacraments, and the host adds: "Became Catholics." Politeo says today that back then "the devil nicely seduced him" with the thought "don't be like everyone else," because he always wanted to be special and different.

sections.subtitle: Bend, rock and roll i život bez Boga
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje razdoblje sviranja u bendu i života bez vjere
sections.content:
Umjesto sakramenata uslijedilo je sviranje u bendu, druženja i, kako sam kaže, „klasične one priče: seks, droga, rock and roll“. Kasnije se zaposlio i, prema današnjim mjerilima, bio je „okej“: savjesno je radio, ispunjavao obaveze i bio pošten.

Sve je to, ističe, živio bez Isusa. Gledajući unatrag, procjenjuje da mu je život tada bio „puno puno teži“ i da mu mnoge stvari nisu bile jasne. U tom je razdoblju imao više partnerica i djevojaka s kojima je živio.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak uglavnom je usklađen jer opisuje prošli način života i izričito ga promatra kao život bez Isusa, a ne kao uzor koji bi slušatelj trebao slijediti. Ipak, izraz „klasična priča” i procjena da je bio „okej” mogu ostaviti dojam blagog uljepšavanja ponašanja koje, ako je uključivalo spolne odnose izvan braka ili zajednički život bez bračne obveze, nije u skladu s katoličkim naukom o spolnosti i braku.
concerns: Spolnost izvan braka može zvučati kao nešto uobičajeno i neproblematično ako se opis ne shvati jasno kao osvrt na prošlost, a ne kao odobravanje.
Pošten rad i ispunjavanje obveza jesu vrijedni, ali sami po sebi ne znače da je čovjekov život u cjelini bio „okej” u moralnom ili duhovnom smislu.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje braka povezuje spolno sjedinjenje s trajnim bračnim savezom i odgovornošću, pa zajednički život bez bračne obveze ne treba prikazivati kao moralno istovjetan braku. Istodobno, pastoralno prosuđivanje razlikuje okolnosti i osobnu odgovornost: opis prošlosti sam po sebi nije opravdavanje, a obraćenje može uključivati iskreno priznanje da život bez Krista nije donosio puninu.
magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned because it describes a past way of life and explicitly views it as a life without Jesus, and not as a model that the listener should follow. Still, the phrase "classic story" and the assessment that he was "okay" may leave the impression of a slight embellishment of behavior which, if it included sexual relations outside of marriage or cohabitation without marital commitment, is not in accordance with Catholic teaching on sexuality and marriage.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of marriage connects sexual union with a permanent marital covenant and responsibility, so cohabitation without marital commitment should not be presented as morally equivalent to marriage. At the same time, pastoral judgment distinguishes between circumstances and personal responsibility: describing the past in itself is not a justification, and conversion can include an honest admission that life without Christ did not bring fullness.
concerns_en: Sexuality outside of marriage can sound like something commonplace and unproblematic if the description is not clearly understood as a reflection on the past rather than approval.
Honest work and fulfilling obligations are valuable, but in themselves they do not mean that a person's life as a whole was "okay" in a moral or spiritual sense.

sections.subtitle_en: Band, rock and roll, and life without God
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes the period of playing in a band and living without faith
sections.content_en:
Instead of the sacraments, what followed was playing in a band, socializing, and, as he himself says, "those classic stories: sex, drugs, rock and roll". Later he got a job and, according to today's standards, he was "okay": he worked conscientiously, fulfilled his obligations, and was honest.

All of this, he emphasizes, he lived without Jesus. Looking back, he assesses that his life then was "much, much harder" and that many things were not clear to him. During that period, he had multiple partners and girlfriends with whom he lived.

sections.subtitle: Pobačaj i spoznaja koja je došla uz usisavač
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Politeo prepričava trenutak kada je shvatio da je pobačajem prekinut život njegova djeteta
sections.content:
S jednom od partnerica Politeo je dobio dijete. Odluku je, kaže, „nažalost prepustio njoj“, jer nije znao bolje. Malo je istraživao na internetu i ostala mu je jedna informacija: veze se nakon pobačaja često raspadnu. Priznaje da ga je najviše brinulo upravo to. Zato je možda i bio skloniji tome da se pobačaj ne napravi, ali tada nije bio svjestan da se time **oduzima ljudski život**.

Pobačaj je ipak izvršen. Nekoliko dana kasnije dogodio se trenutak kojeg se, kako kaže, točno sjeća. Usisavao je stan i odjednom mu je sinulo: „Pa da mi nismo prekinuli taj život, to bi se dijete razvilo, rodilo i bilo bi naše dijete.“ Bila je to prva spoznaja o tome kako su veliku i zlu stvar učinili.

Ta spoznaja nije odmah dovela do obraćenja, nego do raspada veze. Par se sve više udaljavao jer su oboje bježali jedno od drugoga. Razloge je, kaže, razumio tek kasnije, kad je o tome razmatrao u Isusu:

- on je **izgubio povjerenje u žene**;
- ona je izgubila **sigurnost i povjerenje u njega** kao muškarca koji ju je trebao zaštititi;
- zadatak koji su oboje trebali ispuniti ostao je neispunjen.

Zaključuje da se veza bez povjerenja u temelju ne može održati, „pusti ti i strasti i sve“.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je u bitnome usklađen s katoličkim naukom: ispravno prepoznaje pobačaj kao oduzimanje ljudskog života i opisuje ozbiljne posljedice koje su sudionici doživjeli. Ipak, prikaz raspada veze i gubitka povjerenja treba shvatiti kao osobno iskustvo, a ne kao nužnu ili univerzalnu posljedicu pobačaja ni kao potpunu procjenu osobne odgovornosti svakoga sudionika.
concerns: Veza između pobačaja i kasnijeg raspada odnosa prikazana je kroz osobno iskustvo govornika; ne bi je trebalo generalizirati kao ishod koji se događa u svakom paru.

Formulacije o tome da je muškarac trebao zaštititi partnericu i da je on izgubio povjerenje u žene izražavaju njegovu osobnu interpretaciju. Ne treba ih pretvoriti u opću tvrdnju o dužnostima muškaraca i žena niti njima umanjiti vlastitu odgovornost pojedinaca za odluke i postupke.

Odlomak prepoznaje objektivnu težinu pobačaja, ali ne razmatra stupanj osobne krivnje: crkveno prosuđivanje razlikuje moralnu težinu čina od odgovornosti pojedine osobe, koja se prosuđuje uzimajući u obzir konkretne okolnosti.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk uči da je ljudski život svet i nepovrediv od začeća te da se Božja zapovijed „Ne ubij” odnosi i na nerođeno dijete; zato je ispravno pobačaj nazvati oduzimanjem ljudskog života. Istodobno, ozbiljnost čina ne znači da se smije unaprijed jednako procijeniti subjektivna krivnja svih uključenih: Crkva razlikuje objektivni moralni sud od procjene osobne odgovornosti te ranjenima i grešnicima naviješta Božje milosrđe i mogućnost iscjeljenja.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is essentially aligned with Catholic teaching: it correctly recognizes abortion as the taking of human life and describes the serious consequences experienced by the participants. However, the depiction of the breakdown of the relationship and the loss of trust should be understood as a personal experience, and not as a necessary or universal consequence of abortion, nor as a complete assessment of the personal responsibility of each participant.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching teaches that human life is sacred and inviolable from conception, and that God's commandment "You shall not kill" applies also to the unborn child; therefore, it is correct to call abortion the taking of a human life. At the same time, the gravity of the act does not mean that the subjective guilt of all those involved may be judged equally in advance: the Church distinguishes objective moral judgment from the assessment of personal responsibility, and proclaims to the wounded and sinners God's mercy and the possibility of healing.
concerns_en: The connection between abortion and the subsequent breakdown of the relationship is presented through the personal experience of the speaker; it should not be generalized as an outcome that occurs in every couple.

The formulations that the man was supposed to protect his partner and that he lost trust in women express his personal interpretation. They should not be turned into a general claim about the duties of men and women, nor should they diminish the personal responsibility of individuals for their decisions and actions.

The passage recognizes the objective gravity of abortion, but does not consider the degree of personal guilt: ecclesiastical judgment distinguishes the moral gravity of an act from the responsibility of an individual person, which is judged taking into account the concrete circumstances.

sections.subtitle_en: Abortion and the realization that came with a vacuum cleaner
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Politeo recounts the moment when he realized that abortion ended the life of his child
sections.content_en:
With one of his partners, Politeo conceived a child. He says he "unfortunately left the decision to her," because he did not know any better. He researched a bit on the internet and one piece of information stuck with him: relationships often fall apart after an abortion. He admits that this was precisely what worried him the most. That is why he may have been more inclined not to have the abortion, but at the time he was not aware that by doing so **a human life is taken**.

The abortion was nevertheless performed. A few days later, a moment occurred that he says he remembers exactly. He was vacuuming the apartment and it suddenly dawned on him: "Well, if we hadn't ended that life, that child would have developed, been born, and would have been our child." It was the first realization of how great and evil a thing they had done.

That realization did not immediately lead to conversion, but to the breakdown of the relationship. The couple grew further and further apart because both were running away from each other. The reasons, he says, he understood only later, when he reflected on it in Jesus:

- he **lost trust in women**;
- she lost **security and trust in him** as the man who should have protected her;
- the task that both were supposed to fulfill remained unfulfilled.

He concludes that a relationship without trust at its foundation cannot hold up, "leave aside passions and everything."

sections.subtitle: Nevidljiva rana koja je godinama sprječavala nove veze
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava kako ga je iskustvo pobačaja godinama nesvjesno pratilo
sections.content:
Nakon raspada Politeo godinama nije mogao uspostaviti normalnu, funkcionalnu vezu. Iskustvo ga je, kako danas kaže, „proganjalo“, iako tada tako nije razmišljao. Htio je da veza „bude konačno definirana u startu“ jer nije želio sam sebi nanijeti još jednu ranu.

Naglašava da sve to nije bilo svjesno. Da je bilo, vjerojatno bi potražio pomoć. Ranu je prepoznao tek kad je zacijeljela, kada je s djevojkom mogao opet normalno razgovarati i otvoriti se, bez potrebe da sve odmah bude konačno i unaprijed poznato. Sigurnost koja se unaprijed ne može dobiti zamijenio je, kaže, „drugi oslonac“, a to je bio Isus.

magisterium.assessment: Opis je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim razumijevanjem osobnih rana i povjerenja u Krista: prepoznavanje prošle povrede i oslanjanje na Isusa mogu biti važni dijelovi unutarnjeg ozdravljenja. Riječ je o osobnom svjedočanstvu, pa ga ne treba shvatiti kao tvrdnju da se svaka teškoća u odnosima može riješiti samo vjerom ili da se ozdravljenje kod svih odvija na isti način.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveno učenje priznaje da ranija iskustva mogu otežati povjerenje i otvorenost prema drugima te potiče molitvu, prihvaćanje pomoći i osobni rast kao dijelove procesa ozdravljenja. Kristova prisutnost i utjeha u ranama ne isključuju ljudsku pomoć: Crkva se opisuje kao sredstvo koje prati čovjeka na putu prema unutarnjem ozdravljenju i miru srca.
magisterium.assessment_en: The description is largely aligned with the Catholic understanding of personal wounds and trust in Christ: recognizing a past hurt and relying on Jesus can be important parts of inner healing. This is a personal testimony, so it should not be taken as an assertion that every relationship difficulty can be resolved through faith alone or that healing occurs in the same way for everyone.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Church teaching recognizes that past experiences can make trust and openness toward others difficult, and it encourages prayer, accepting help, and personal growth as parts of the healing process. Christ's presence and comfort in wounds do not exclude human help: the Church is described as a means that accompanies man on the path toward inner healing and peace of heart.

sections.subtitle_en: The invisible wound that prevented new relationships for years
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains how the experience of abortion unconsciously followed him for years
sections.content_en:
After the breakup, for years Politeo was unable to establish a normal, functional relationship. The experience, as he says today, "haunted" him, although back then he did not think that way. He wanted the relationship to "be definitively defined at the start" because he did not want to inflict another wound upon himself.

He emphasizes that all this was not conscious. If it had been, he probably would have sought help. He recognized the wound only when it had healed, when he was able to talk normally with a girlfriend again and open up, without the need for everything to be definitive and known in advance right away. The certainty that cannot be obtained in advance was replaced, he says, by "another support", and that was Jesus.

sections.subtitle: Prvi vapaj Bogu: „Ja sam bitan“
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Politeo prepričava unutarnje iskustvo riječi „Ja sam bitan“
sections.content:
Pet ili šest godina nakon pobačaja na poslu se zakomplicirala jedna situacija. Politeo nije bio kriv, ali je sve upućivalo na to da će krivnja pasti na njega. „Najteže je kad si nevino osuđen“, kaže.

Tada je prvi put zavapio Bogu: „Gospodine, evo, nikad Te nisam ništa žicao, hajde sad Ti uđi u moj život i riješi ovu situaciju, jer ja više sam ne mogu.“

Gospodin ju je riješio, ali ne onako kako je on htio. Situacija se najprije dodatno zakomplicirala. U tom trenutku nešto mu se, kaže, prelomilo u srcu i iznutra je čuo ili osjetio: „Vidiš da je to sve nebitno, **Ja sam bitan**.“ Odgovorio je: „Pa da, Gospodine, Ti si bitan“ i prepustio stvar riječima „Nek' bude šta bude“.

Dan ili dva kasnije cijela se situacija rasplinula i ništa nije bilo onako dramatično kako je izgledalo. Ostalo mu je iskustvo: „Ja sam bitan.“

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: prepoznaje Božji primat i prikazuje predanje Bogu kao čin povjerenja, a ne kao zahtjev da Bog odmah riješi teškoću na željeni način. Iskustvo unutarnje poruke može biti osobno značajno, ali samo po sebi ne dokazuje da je riječ o Božjoj objavi.
concerns: Izraz „čuo ili osjetio” treba razumjeti kao osobno iskustvo koje valja razborito prosuđivati, a ne automatski poistovjetiti s Božjim govorom.
Kasniji povoljan rasplet ne treba tumačiti kao jamstvo da će Bog uvijek ukloniti nepravdu ili riješiti svaku krizu na vidljiv način.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička duhovnost povezuje povjerenje u Boga s predanjem njegovoj volji i providnosti: vjernik se može pouzdati u njegovu očinsku brigu i onda kada se okolnosti ne odvijaju kako želi. Biblijska i crkvena tradicija istodobno potvrđuju dostojanstvo svake osobe kao ljubljene od Boga; zato „Ti si bitan” može izraziti ispravno preusmjeravanje s vlastite krize na Boga, bez zaključka da čovjek sam po sebi nema vrijednost.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching: it recognizes the primacy of God and presents surrender to God as an act of trust, rather than a demand that God immediately resolve the difficulty in the desired way. The experience of an inner message may be personally significant, but in itself does not prove that it is a divine revelation.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic spirituality links trust in God with surrender to His will and providence: the believer can rely on His fatherly care even when circumstances do not unfold as desired. At the same time, biblical and Church tradition affirm the dignity of every person as beloved by God; therefore, "You are important" can express a correct redirection from one's own crisis to God, without concluding that man in himself has no worth.
concerns_en: The phrase "heard or felt" should be understood as a personal experience that ought to be judged prudently, rather than automatically equated with God speaking.
The subsequent favorable outcome should not be interpreted as a guarantee that God will always remove injustice or resolve every crisis in a visible way.

sections.subtitle_en: The First Cry to God: "I Am Important"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Politeo recounts the inner experience of the words "I Am Important"
sections.content_en:
Five or six years after the abortion, a situation at work became complicated. Politeo was not at fault, but everything indicated that the blame would fall on him. "It is hardest when you are condemned innocently," he says.

Then he cried out to God for the first time: "Lord, look, I have never begged You for anything, come now into my life and resolve this situation, because I can no longer do it alone."

The Lord resolved it, but not in the way he wanted. At first, the situation became even more complicated. At that moment, he says, something broke in his heart and from within he heard or felt: "You see that it is all unimportant, **I am important**." He replied: "Well yes, Lord, You are important" and left the matter with the words "Whatever happens, happens."

A day or two later, the entire situation dissolved and nothing was as dramatic as it had seemed. What remained with him was the experience: "I am important."

sections.subtitle: Sakramenti kod Svetog Josipa na Trešnjevci i poziv na služenje
sections.screenshot_description: Gost citira Evanđelje o Sinu Čovječjem koji je došao služiti
sections.content:
Nakon toga Politeo se obratio jedinoj prijateljici iz društva koja je redovito išla u crkvu, a koja mu je danas krsna kuma: „Hajde idem s tobom u crkvu, hajmo krenuti u crkvu zajedno.“ Počeo je odlaziti na nedjeljne mise u crkvu **Svetog Josipa na Trešnjevci** i primio sakramente.

Tako je počeo njegov obraćenički život: slušanje propovijedi i čitanje Riječi Božje. Posebno ga je dotaknuo redak koji pripisuje Marku (Mk 10,45), uz koji spominje i Mateja: „Ni Sin Čovječji nije došao da bude služen, nego da služi i da život svoj dade kao otkupninu za mnoge.“

Poruku o služenju čuo je posvuda. Shvatio je da je, nakon što je upoznao Gospodina i postao svjestan koliko je toga primio na dar, došlo vrijeme da služi. Zato je molio: „Gospodine, Ti mi pokaži gdje ću služiti.“

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je u skladu s katoličkim naukom: obraćenje, slušanje Evanđelja i želja da se služi prikazani su kao odgovor na Božji dar i Kristov poziv, a navod o Sinu Čovječjem vjerno prenosi Mk 10,45 i Mt 20,28. Nema bitnog teološkog problema; spominjanje primanja sakramenata ostaje općenito, pa se bez dodatnih pojedinosti ne mogu procijeniti okolnosti ni sakramentalna priprema.
magisterium.enrichment: Kršćansko obraćenje nije samo odluka da se čovjek ponaša bolje, nego vjera koja uključuje život u zajedništvu s Kristom i traje kroz svakodnevno nasljedovanje; sakramenti pomirenja i euharistije osobito podupiru taj put. Isusova služba nije tek općenita ljubaznost: ona seže do predanja života na križu, a kršćansko služenje poziva učenike da slijede taj uzor. Molitva da mu Gospodin pokaže gdje će služiti prikladno izražava stav razlučivanja: kršćanska služba i crkveno poslanje razumiju se kao odgovor na Božji poziv, a ne kao samostalni projekt ili osobna ambicija.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is in accordance with Catholic teaching: conversion, listening to the Gospel, and the desire to serve are presented as a response to God's gift and Christ's call, and the quote about the Son of Man faithfully conveys Mk 10:45 and Mt 20:28. There is no essential theological issue; the mention of receiving the sacraments remains general, so without additional details, neither the circumstances nor the sacramental preparation can be assessed.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Christian conversion is not merely a decision to behave better, but faith that includes a life in communion with Christ and lasts through daily following; the sacraments of reconciliation and the Eucharist especially support that path. Jesus' ministry is not merely general kindness: it extends to the surrender of his life on the cross, and Christian service calls disciples to follow that example. The prayer asking that the Lord show him where he will serve fittingly expresses an attitude of discernment: Christian ministry and ecclesial mission are understood as a response to God's call, and not as an independent project or personal ambition.

sections.subtitle_en: Sacraments at Sveti Josip na Trešnjevci and the call to service
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest quotes the Gospel about the Son of Man who came to serve
sections.content_en:
After that, Politeo turned to the only friend from his circle who regularly went to church, and who is today his baptismal godmother: "Come on, I'm going with you to church, let's start going to church together." He began going to Sunday Masses at the church of **Sveti Josip na Trešnjevci** and received the sacraments.

Thus began his convert life: listening to homilies and reading the Word of God. He was particularly touched by the verse that he attributes to Mark (Mk 10:45), alongside which he also mentions Matthew: "Not even the Son of Man came to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many."

He heard the message about serving everywhere. He realized that, after he came to know the Lord and became aware of how much he had received as a gift, the time had come to serve. Therefore he prayed: "Lord, You show me where I will serve."

sections.subtitle: „40 dana za život“ sa svih strana
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Politeo opisuje kako je posvuda nailazio na poziv inicijative „40 dana za život“
sections.content:
Odgovor je, kaže, stigao vrlo brzo. Kad bi upalio radio, čuo bi „40 dana za život“. Kad bi došao na misu, **Ante Čaljkušić** predstavljao je inicijativu i najavljivao prvu kampanju. Poziv je dolazio „sa svih strana“.

Nije poznavao nikoga iz inicijative, jer osim njegove kume nitko iz njegova društva nije išao u crkvu. Bilo mu je teško. Mučilo ga je pitanje hoće li naići na osudu, „jer i ja sam taj koji je napravio pobačaj“. Ipak je odlučio „ići u nepoznato“.

U prve dvije kampanje dolazio je na bdjenja. U trećoj ga je, kako kaže, Duh Sveti stalno poticao da učini više. Nazvao je i javila mu se **Petra**, današnja direktorica inicijative, s pozivom: „Dođi na sastanak, pa vidjet ćemo.“ Tako je počeo njegov aktivni angažman.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom potpuno usklađen s katoličkim razumijevanjem obraćenja, milosrđa i služenja životu: prikazuje osobu koja, unatoč strahu od osude, ulazi u zajednicu i postupno se uključuje u apostolat. Ne umanjuje ozbiljnost pobačaja niti tvrdi da je njegovo iskustvo samo po sebi dokaz posebne objave; opisuje osobno prepoznavanje poticaja Duha Svetoga.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički odgovor na pobačaj istodobno čuva istinu da je riječ o teškoj nepravdi i nadu da su obraćenje, oproštenje i mir mogući; Crkva također poziva na duhovnu i psihološku potporu osobama koje su pogođene tim iskustvom. Papa Benedikt XVI. podsjeća da takva iskustva mogu voditi i služenju zaštiti ljudskog života, ali to ne znači da se nečija bol ili odgovornost smiju pojednostaviti niti da je javni angažman zamjena za osobno ozdravljenje i pomirenje s Bogom.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely fully aligned with the Catholic understanding of conversion, mercy, and service to life: it depicts a person who, despite the fear of condemnation, enters a community and gradually becomes involved in the apostolate. It does not diminish the gravity of abortion, nor does it claim that his experience in itself is proof of a special revelation; it describes a personal recognition of the promptings of the Holy Spirit.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic response to abortion simultaneously preserves the truth that it is a grave injustice and the hope that conversion, forgiveness, and peace are possible; the Church also calls for spiritual and psychological support for persons affected by that experience. Pope Benedict XVI reminds us that such experiences can also lead to service in protecting human life, but this does not mean that someone's pain or responsibility may be simplified, nor that public involvement is a substitute for personal healing and reconciliation with God.

sections.subtitle_en: “40 Days for Life” from all sides
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Politeo describes how he encountered the invitation of the “40 Days for Life” initiative everywhere
sections.content_en:
The answer, he says, arrived very quickly. Whenever he turned on the radio, he would hear “40 Days for Life”. Whenever he came to Mass, **Ante Čaljkušić** was presenting the initiative and announcing the first campaign. The call was coming “from all sides”.

He did not know anyone from the initiative, because except for his godmother, no one from his circle went to church. It was hard for him. He was troubled by the question of whether he would encounter condemnation, “because I too am the one who had an abortion.” Still, he decided “to go into the unknown”.

In the first two campaigns, he came to vigils. In the third, as he says, the Holy Spirit constantly prompted him to do more. He called, and **Petra**, today's director of the initiative, answered with the invitation: “Come to a meeting, and we'll see.” That is how his active involvement began.

sections.subtitle: Ne iz dužnosti, nego iz milosti oprosta
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava da u inicijativu nije ušao kako bi okajao pobačaj
sections.content:
Voditelj postavlja osjetljivo pitanje: je li Politea u inicijativu dovelo upravo iskustvo pobačaja, možda kao potreba da ga opravda? Pojašnjava da ne tvrdi da je tako, ali zna ljude koji nakon pobačaja smatraju da tu ranu moraju „oprati“ molitvom ispred bolnica i domova zdravlja, kao zadovoljštinu za grijeh koji je Bog već davno oprostio.

Politeo odgovara niječno. Imao je, kaže, **milost da je u ispovijedi uoči prve pričesti zaista sve ispovjedio** i dobio Božji oprost. Gospodinu je dužan „za sve“, ali ne zbog tog grijeha. Pobačaj mu se, štoviše, činio kao moguća prepreka. U inicijativu je otišao jer je tražio Gospodina, a On je pokazivao u tom smjeru.

Osjetio je kako je s njega skinuto „ogromno breme“ i nikada nije imao potrebu taj grijeh ponovno ispovijedati. Žali, naravno, kad se sjeti, ali ističe da ostajanje u prošlosti nema smisla. Prošlost mu danas služi kao podsjetnik i kao iskustvo koje mu pomaže **razumjeti polaznike programa**. Oni se lakše otvaraju kad znaju da je pred njima jednako grešan čovjek koji ih neće osuđivati.

Prvi put se pred članovima inicijative otvorio na zajedničkoj duhovnoj obnovi. Svi su ga, kaže, prihvatili s ljubavlju i nije bilo osude. Bilo im je drago što je netko s takvim iskustvom došao među njih kao plod ljubavi i molitve.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: sakramentalno odrješenje donosi stvarni oprost, a kršćanska služba može proizići iz zahvalnosti i milosti, a ne iz pokušaja da se Božje oproštenje zasluži. Važno je ipak ne poistovjetiti oproštenje s time da su nevažni kajanje, pokora ili moguća potreba za pomirenjem i ozdravljenjem.
concerns: Izraz da čovjek nakon oproštenja nema što više činiti mogao bi se pogrešno razumjeti kao nijekanje pokore ili plodova obraćenja; odlomak to izričito ne tvrdi, ali korisno je razlikovati Božje oproštenje od procesa ozdravljenja i popravljanja posljedica grijeha.
magisterium.enrichment: Iskreno ispovijedanje i primljeno odrješenje opravdavaju govor o stvarnom oproštenju; crkveni izvor pritom potvrđuje da je oproštenje dostupno obraćenom grešniku, ali i naglašava da je pobačaj težak grijeh jer oduzima život nedužnoj osobi. Biblijska slika izgubljene ovce pokazuje Božju inicijativu i radost zbog obraćenja, dok Evanđelje poziva na obraćenje i oproštenje; zato služenje drugima može biti plod primljene milosti, a ne način da se ona kupi.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching: sacramental absolution brings real forgiveness, and Christian ministry can flow from gratitude and grace, not from an attempt to earn God's forgiveness. It is important, however, not to equate forgiveness with repentance, penance, or the possible need for reconciliation and healing being unimportant.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Sincere confession and received absolution justify speaking of real forgiveness; the church source affirms that forgiveness is available to the converted sinner, but also emphasizes that abortion is a grave sin because it takes the life of an innocent person. The biblical image of the lost sheep demonstrates God's initiative and joy over conversion, while the Gospel calls to repentance and forgiveness; therefore, serving others can be the fruit of received grace, not a way to purchase it.
concerns_en: The expression that a person has nothing more to do after forgiveness could be misunderstood as a denial of penance or the fruits of conversion; the passage does not explicitly claim this, but it is useful to distinguish God's forgiveness from the process of healing and repairing the consequences of sin.

sections.subtitle_en: Not out of duty, but out of the grace of forgiveness
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains that he did not enter the initiative to atone for abortion
sections.content_en:
The host asks a sensitive question: did the experience of abortion bring Politeo to the initiative, perhaps as a need to justify it? He clarifies that he is not claiming that this is so, but he knows people who, after an abortion, consider that they must "wash" that wound through prayer in front of hospitals and health centers, as satisfaction for a sin that God has already forgiven long ago.

Politeo answers negatively. He had, he says, **the grace that in confession on the eve of First Communion he truly confessed everything** and received God's forgiveness. He is indebted to the Lord "for everything", but not because of that sin. Abortion, moreover, seemed to him like a possible obstacle. He went into the initiative because he was seeking the Lord, and He was pointing in that direction.

He felt that an "enormous burden" was lifted from him and he never had a need to confess that sin again. He regrets it, of course, when he remembers, but emphasizes that staying in the past makes no sense. Today, the past serves him as a reminder and as an experience that helps him **understand the program participants**. They open up more easily when they know that before them stands an equally sinful man who will not judge them.

He opened up before the members of the initiative for the first time at a joint spiritual retreat. Everyone, he says, accepted him with love and there was no judgment. They were glad that someone with such an experience came among them as a fruit of love and prayer.

sections.subtitle: Više od deset godina u „teškom duhovnom boju“
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Politeo govori o kapi u oceanu i licima spašene djece
sections.content:
Voditelj podsjeća da je Politeo u inicijativi od 2014., dakle više od deset godina, te da je riječ o „teškom duhovnom boju“ punom protivljenja. Pita ga što ga drži da ne odustane.

Politeo objašnjava da se u zahtjevnijim životnim razdobljima zna povući korak unatrag. Umjesto da vodi zagrebački tim, preuzme manji dio posla, primjerice koordinaciju bdjenja, jer je pozvan davati vrijeme i obitelji. Na potpuni odlazak, međutim, nikada nije ozbiljno pomišljao, iako mu takva misao zna „proletjeti kroz glavu“.

Razlog je to što zna koliko je taj rad vrijedan i koliko je života spasio, ne samo djece nego i majki i očeva koji su napravili pobačaj ili o njemu razmišljali. Citira **Majku Terezijom**: to možda jest samo kap u oceanu, ali bez te kapi ocean bi bio siromašniji. Ističe da to za njega više nije samo kap: „Ti znaš te ljude, ti vidiš ta lica, ti upoznaš tu djecu.“ Svjestan je da te djece ne bi bilo i da bi roditelji bili ranjeni da netko nije bio ondje. Taj netko slučajno je bio on, a bez njega možda ne bi bio nitko.

magisterium.assessment: Opis ustrajnog zauzimanja za nerođene i pomaganja majkama i očevima uglavnom je u skladu s katoličkim naukom o zaštiti ljudskog života od začeća te potrebi konkretne potpore obiteljima i ženama u teškim trudnoćama. Naglasak na obiteljskim obvezama također je razborit, dok izjava da bi bez njega možda „ne bi bio nitko“ traži nijansiranje kako se služenje ne bi prikazalo kao osobno nezamjenjivo.
concerns: Tvrdnju da bi bez njega možda nitko ne bio ondje bolje je razumjeti kao osobni doživljaj važnosti služenja, a ne kao sigurnu procjenu da je on bio nezamjenjiv ili jedini moguć posrednik pomoći.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveni nauk ne svodi apostolat za život samo na protivljenje pobačaju, nego ističe i izgradnju: pružanje prihvaćanja, pomoći i potpore roditeljima te pomoć ženama koje su imale pobačaj. U tom se smislu opis bdjenja i susreta s konkretnim obiteljima može razumjeti kao djelo ljubavi prema bližnjemu i obrane dostojanstva nerođenoga; Ivan Pavao II. izričito je pohvalio i zauzimanje protiv pobačaja i pomoć majkama kao prihvatljivu alternativu. Ustrajnost u služenju može biti plod vjernosti, ali razborito smanjenje opsega odgovornosti radi obitelji nije odustajanje od dobra: kršćansko služenje treba ostati usklađeno s konkretnim dužnostima i ograničenjima osobe.

magisterium.assessment_en: The description of persevering advocacy for the unborn and helping mothers and fathers is generally in accordance with Catholic teaching on the protection of human life from conception and the need for concrete support for families and women in difficult pregnancies. The emphasis on family obligations is also prudent, while the statement that without him perhaps "no one would have been there" requires nuance so that service is not portrayed as personally irreplaceable.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Church teaching does not reduce the pro-life apostolate solely to opposition to abortion, but also emphasizes edification: providing acceptance, help, and support to parents and assistance to women who have had an abortion. In that sense, the description of vigils and encounters with concrete families can be understood as an act of charity toward one's neighbor and defense of the dignity of the unborn; John Paul II explicitly praised both advocacy against abortion and assistance to mothers as an acceptable alternative. Perseverance in service can be a fruit of faithfulness, but a prudent reduction in the scope of responsibilities for the sake of the family is not giving up on doing good: Christian service must remain aligned with a person's concrete duties and limitations.
concerns_en: The claim that without him perhaps no one would have been there is better understood as a personal experience of the importance of service, rather than as a certain assessment that he was irreplaceable or the only possible mediator of help.

sections.subtitle_en: More than ten years in a "difficult spiritual battle"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Politeo speaks about a drop in the ocean and the faces of saved children
sections.content_en:
The host reminds that Politeo has been in the initiative since 2014, meaning more than ten years, and that it is a "difficult spiritual battle" full of opposition. He asks him what keeps him from giving up.

Politeo explains that during more demanding periods of life, he knows to take a step back. Instead of leading the Zagreb team, he takes on a smaller share of the work, for example coordinating vigils, because he is called to give time to family as well. However, he has never seriously thought about leaving completely, although such a thought can "flash through his head".

The reason is that he knows how valuable this work is and how many lives it has saved, not only of children but also of mothers and fathers who had an abortion or were considering it. He quotes **Mother Teresa**: it may be just a drop in the ocean, but without that drop the ocean would be poorer. He points out that for him it is no longer just a drop: "You know those people, you see those faces, you get to know those children." He is aware that those children would not exist and that the parents would be wounded if someone had not been there. That someone happened to be him, and without him perhaps no one would have been there.

sections.subtitle: Prva molitva ispred bolnice i lekcija Šimuna Cirenca
sections.screenshot_description: Gost uspoređuje molitelje ispred bolnica sa Šimunom Cirencem
sections.content:
Prvi izlazak na molitvu ispred bolnice bio je, priznaje Politeo, nezgodan, „to svatko tko je ikad išao moliti ispred bolnice može svjedočiti“. Razmišljao je o tome što će drugi reći i tko bi ga mogao vidjeti.

S vremenom su ti **ljudski obziri** nestali, jer zna zašto je ondje. Pomoglo mu je i to što je naučio argumentirati. Preporučuje knjigu **„Uvjerljivo za život“**, a voditelj dodaje da postoje dva takva izdanja. Iz njih se, kaže, čovjek može „oboružati“ informacijama i naučiti razgovarati s ljudima, pa mu više nije neugodno reći: „Stojim tu da bih obranio ove najmanje.“

Potrebu za prisutnošću na licu mjesta objašnjava primjerom **Šimuna Cirenca**: ne bi mogao ponijeti Isusov križ da je u tom trenutku molio u sinagogi, nego je morao biti ondje gdje je bio Isus. Isto vrijedi i danas: „Gdje su majke i očevi koji idu na pobačaj, tamo moramo biti. Neće oni nas doći tražiti po kapelicama.“

Kako je sve više ljudi znalo za njegov angažman, bio je spreman u miru razgovarati sa svakim tko to želi. Kad naiđe na „zid koji samo puca informacije“, zaustavi se, jer nema smisla prepucavati se s nekim tko ne želi razgovarati.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: promiče zaštitu nerođenih, osobno svjedočenje i miran dijalog, a Šimuna Cirenca koristi kao prikladnu analogiju za blizinu onima koji trpe. Ipak, ta analogija sama po sebi ne uspostavlja obvezu da svaki vjernik bude prisutan ispred bolnice niti opravdava pritisak ili uznemiravanje.
concerns: Izraz „tamo moramo biti” valja razumjeti kao poziv na razborito i nenasilno svjedočenje, a ne kao bezuvjetnu obvezu svakog vjernika ili dopuštenje za prisilu, zastrašivanje ili nepoštovanje dostojanstva majke i oca.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko svjedočenje za život uključuje i obrazlaganje stava i praktičnu pomoć trudnicama, djeci i obiteljima; zato obrana nerođenoga treba biti povezana sa suosjećanjem i konkretnom podrškom. Crkveni izvori potiču zaštitu života i navode da se život brani nenasilnim sredstvima kad god je to moguće.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching: it promotes the protection of the unborn, personal witness, and peaceful dialogue, and uses Simon of Cyrene as an appropriate analogy for closeness to those who suffer. However, this analogy in itself does not establish an obligation for every believer to be present in front of a hospital, nor does it justify pressure or harassment.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic witness for life includes both explaining one's stance and practical assistance to pregnant women, children, and families; therefore, the defense of the unborn should be connected with compassion and concrete support. Church sources encourage the protection of life and state that life is defended by nonviolent means whenever possible.
concerns_en: The phrase “that is where we must be” should be understood as a call to prudent and nonviolent witness, and not as an unconditional obligation of every believer or permission for coercion, intimidation, or disrespect for the dignity of the mother and father.

sections.subtitle_en: The First Prayer in Front of the Hospital and the Lesson of Simon of Cyrene
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest compares those praying in front of hospitals to Simon of Cyrene
sections.content_en:
The first time going out to pray in front of the hospital was, Politeo admits, awkward, “anyone who has ever gone to pray in front of a hospital can testify to that.” He thought about what others would say and who might see him.

Over time, these **human considerations** disappeared, because he knows why he is there. It also helped him that he learned how to make arguments. He recommends the book **“Persuasive for Life”**, and the host adds that there are two such editions. From them, he says, one can “arm” oneself with information and learn to speak with people, so it is no longer uncomfortable for him to say: “I stand here to defend these least ones.”

He explains the need for presence on site through the example of **Simon of Cyrene**: he would not have been able to carry Jesus' cross if he had been praying in the synagogue at that moment, but rather he had to be where Jesus was. The same applies today: “Where mothers and fathers who are going for an abortion are, that is where we must be. They will not come looking for us in chapels.”

As more and more people knew about his involvement, he was ready to speak in peace with anyone who wanted to. When he encounters a “wall that only fires information,” he stops, because there is no point in bickering with someone who does not want to converse.

sections.subtitle: Čuda koja se ne mogu opisati: od depresije do radosti
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Politeo opisuje muškarca koji je nakon dvadeset godina oprostio sebi
sections.content:
Najsnažniji poticaj Politeu su čuda kojima svjedoči. Opisuje muškarca koji dvadeset godina nije mogao oprostiti sam sebi, a nakon programa je to uspio. „Ne zbog mene, nego zbog Gospodina, ali bio sam tu prisutan i vidio sam to čudo čovjeka koji je oživio.“

Takva iskustva, kaže, daju snagu i potvrdu da su na pravom putu jer „Gospodin čini čuda, čini ih danas, čini ih posvuda“. Priznaje i da se ponekad, unatoč svemu, pita ima li sve to smisla. Takve misli pripisuje Zlome, a brzo se vraća spoznaji da je svjedočio neopisivim čudima, „da čovjek iz depresije ide u radost“.

Voditelj dodaje da ljudi brzo zaborave čuda pa im uvijek iznova treba novi poticaj.

magisterium.assessment: Svjedočenje o Božjem djelovanju, oprostu i obnovljenoj radosti uglavnom je u skladu s kršćanskom vjerom: evanđeoska čuda objavljuju Božju milosrdnu ljubav, a vjera može biti povezana s ozdravljenjem. Ipak, odlomak ne daje dovoljno podataka da bi se nečije iskustvo moglo prosuditi kao čudo u strogom smislu niti da bi se povremene sumnje sigurno pripisale Zlome.
concerns: Pripisivanje sumnji Zlome izrečeno je kategorički; za takvu duhovnu prosudbu potreban je oprez, jer sumnje mogu imati različite uzroke i same po sebi ne dokazuju napastovanje.
Izraz „iz depresije ide u radost” može opisivati stvaran duhovni ili emocionalni pomak, ali ne bi ga trebalo razumjeti kao dokaz da je depresija izliječena ili da je uvijek riječ o nadnaravnom čudu.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveno učenje prepoznaje čuda kao znakove Božje spasenjske ljubavi, a ne samo kao izvanredne događaje; zato je primjereno svjedočiti o njima s zahvalnošću i poniznošću. Radost može pratiti susret s Kristom, ali kršćanski život uključuje i žalost, tjeskobu i patnju, pa prisutnost depresije ili tuge ne treba automatski tumačiti kao udaljenost od Boga.

citations.document_title: General Audience of 28 September 2022 - Catechesis On Discernment: 3. The elements of discernment. Familiarity with the Lord

magisterium.assessment_en: The testimony about God's action, forgiveness, and renewed joy is generally in accordance with the Christian faith: evangelical miracles reveal God's merciful love, and faith can be connected with healing. Nevertheless, the passage does not provide enough data for someone's experience to be judged as a miracle in the strict sense, nor for occasional doubts to be attributed with certainty to the Evil One.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Church teaching recognizes miracles as signs of God's salvific love, and not merely as extraordinary events; therefore it is appropriate to witness to them with gratitude and humility. Joy can accompany an encounter with Christ, but Christian life also includes sorrow, anxiety, and suffering, so the presence of depression or sadness should not be automatically interpreted as distance from God.
concerns_en: Attributing doubts to the Evil One is expressed categorically; caution is required for such spiritual discernment, because doubts can have various causes and by themselves do not prove temptation.

The expression „goes from depression into joy” can describe a real spiritual or emotional shift, but it should not be understood as proof that depression has been cured or that it is always a matter of a supernatural miracle.

sections.subtitle_en: Miracles that cannot be described: from depression to joy
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Politeo describes a man who forgave himself after twenty years
sections.content_en:
The strongest incentive for Politeo is the miracles he witnesses. He describes a man who for twenty years could not forgive himself, and after the program he succeeded. „Not because of me, but because of the Lord, but I was present there and I saw that miracle of a man who came back to life.“

Such experiences, he says, give strength and confirmation that they are on the right path because „the Lord works miracles, He works them today, He works them everywhere.“ He also admits that sometimes, despite everything, he wonders whether all of this makes sense. He attributes such thoughts to the Evil One, and quickly returns to the realization that he has witnessed indescribable miracles, „that a man goes from depression into joy.“

The host adds that people quickly forget miracles, so time and again they need a new incentive.

sections.subtitle: Kava koju nije popio i krunica koja je promijenila sve
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prepričava jutro kada je ispred Vinogradske bolnice upoznao suprugu Antoniju
sections.content:
Na pitanje o najvećem plodu molitve za nerođene Politeo odgovara da bi mu bez inicijative cijeli život bio drugačiji, a najvidljiviji je dokaz njegova supruga. **Antoniju je upoznao na mjestu bdjenja.**

Priču pripovijeda u detaljima. Imao je noćnu smjenu s petka na subotu, otprilike od dva do četiri sata ujutro. Nakon nekoliko sati sna, oko devet ujutro, skuhao je kavu i namjeravao je popiti u miru. Tada je živio u **Kranjčevićevoj**, nedaleko od **Vinogradske bolnice**. U grupi se pojavila poruka da ispred Vinogradske neka žena treba pomoć. Čekao je hoće li se netko drugi javiti jer je tek bio došao kući. Na kraju je rekao: „Dobro, hajde, Gospodine, idem ja, neću popiti kavu.“

S gospođom je proveo petnaestak do dvadeset minuta i riješio što je trebalo. Budući da je već bio ondje, odlučio je izmoliti još jednu krunicu. Molio ju je s djevojkom koju dotad nije poznavao, Antonijom. Bila je to njihova prva zajednička krunica.

Tjedan dana kasnije pozvao ju je na tribinu, „kao što zovem sve ljude“, a potom je došla i na konferenciju. Voditelj se prisjeća da su „tamo pali i ćevapi“, a Politeo potvrđuje i dodaje da je i voditelj tada bio prisutan. Uslijedili su izlasci, upoznavanje i vjenčanje.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: prikazuje molitvu krunice, služenje drugoj osobi i nastanak braka kao važne dijelove osobne životne priče, bez iznošenja tvrdnje koja bi proturječila vjeri ili Svetom pismu. Ipak, susret i kasniji brak prikazani su kao osobno iskustvo, pa ih ne treba uzimati kao dokaz da molitva uvijek vodi određenom ishodu.
magisterium.enrichment: Krunica je katolička molitva koja može podupirati razmatranje i vjernost, ali njezina se vrijednost ne mjeri time hoće li donijeti određeni zemaljski rezultat. Katoličko razumijevanje providnosti dopušta prepoznavanje Božjeg djelovanja u običnim događajima i odnosima, ali ne zahtijeva da se svaki detalj životne priče proglasi izravnim čudom ili sigurnim znakom Božje volje.

citations.document_title: Message to those taking part in the recitation of the Rosary (February 6, 1999)

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching: it presents the prayer of the Rosary, service to another person, and the beginning of a marriage as important parts of a personal life story, without making any claim that would contradict the faith or Sacred Scripture. Nevertheless, the meeting and subsequent marriage are presented as a personal experience, so they should not be taken as proof that prayer always leads to a specific outcome.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Rosary is a Catholic prayer that can support contemplation and fidelity, but its value is not measured by whether it will bring a specific earthly result. The Catholic understanding of providence allows the recognition of God's action in ordinary events and relationships, but does not require that every detail of a life story be declared a direct miracle or a certain sign of God's will.

sections.subtitle_en: The coffee he didn't drink and the Rosary that changed everything
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recounts the morning when he met his wife Antonija in front of Vinogradska bolnica
sections.content_en:
To the question about the greatest fruit of prayer for the unborn, Politeo answers that without the initiative his entire life would have been different, and the most visible proof is his wife. **He met Antonija at the vigil site.**

He tells the story in detail. He had a night shift from Friday to Saturday, approximately from two to four in the morning. After a few hours of sleep, around nine in the morning, he brewed coffee and intended to drink it in peace. At that time he lived in **Kranjčevićeva**, not far from **Vinogradska bolnica**. A message appeared in the group that in front of Vinogradska a woman needed help. He waited to see if someone else would respond because he had just arrived home. In the end, he said: „Alright, come on, Lord, I'm going, I won't drink the coffee.“

He spent about fifteen to twenty minutes with the lady and resolved what was needed. Since he was already there, he decided to pray another Rosary. He prayed it with a girl he had not known until then, Antonija. It was their first Rosary together.

A week later he invited her to a panel discussion, „like I invite all people“, and then she also came to the conference. The host recalls that „they also had ćevapi there“, and Politeo confirms and adds that the host was also present then. Dating, getting to know each other, and marriage followed.

sections.subtitle: Ekskluziva u studiju: dijete na putu
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj se iznenađeno raduje vijesti o djetetu koje dolazi
sections.content:
Govoreći o obitelji, Politeo navodi da on i Antonija danas imaju **tri rođena sina, jedno dijete na nebu i bebu koja dolazi**.

Voditelj je iznenađen: „Opa, to je nešto novo. To mi se nisi pohvalio.“ Politeo odgovara da još nije, „evo sad ti se hvalimo“. Voditelj vijest proglašava ekskluzivom i čestita mu.

magisterium.assessment: Izjava radosno prihvaća obitelj i dolazak novoga djeteta te je u skladu s katoličkim pogledom na djecu kao Božji dar. Izraz „dijete na nebu” može se razumjeti kao izraz kršćanske nade i utjehe, ali ne treba ga prikazivati kao sigurnu tvrdnju o sudbini djeteta ako okolnosti smrti nisu poznate.
concerns: Moguća je teološka nepreciznost ako se izraz „dijete na nebu” shvati kao tvrdnja da Crkva jamči spasenje svakog djeteta koje je umrlo bez krštenja; katolički nauk takvu sudbinu povjerava Božjem milosrđu i izražava nadu, a ne konačnu sigurnost.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička vjera potiče roditelje da novo dijete prihvate kao Božji dar i odgovorno ga štite od začeća nadalje. Za djecu koja umru bez krštenja Crkva naglašava, s jedne strane, krštenja nužnost i, s druge, nadu u Božje spasenje milosrđe; zato je govor o „djetetu na nebu” prikladan kao nada i utjeha, uz poniznost pred otajstvom Božjeg suda.

citations.document_title: The Hope of Salvation for Infants Who Die without Being Baptised

magisterium.assessment_en: The statement joyfully accepts family and the arrival of a new child and is in accordance with the Catholic view of children as God's gift. The phrase „child in heaven” can be understood as an expression of Christian hope and comfort, but it should not be presented as a certain claim about the fate of the child if the circumstances of death are not known.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic faith encourages parents to accept a new child as God's gift and responsibly protect it from conception onwards. For children who die without baptism, the Church emphasizes, on the one hand, the necessity of baptism and, on the other, hope in God's saving mercy; therefore, speaking of a „child in heaven” is appropriate as hope and comfort, with humility before the mystery of God's judgment.
concerns_en: Theological imprecision is possible if the phrase „child in heaven” is understood as a claim that the Church guarantees the salvation of every child who died without baptism; Catholic teaching entrusts such a fate to God's mercy and expresses hope, rather than definitive certainty.

sections.subtitle_en: Exclusive in the studio: a child on the way
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host rejoices in surprise at the news of the child that is coming
sections.content_en:
Speaking about family, Politeo states that he and Antonija today have **three born sons, one child in heaven, and a baby that is coming**.

The host is surprised: „Whoa, that's something new. You didn't brag about that to me.“ Politeo responds that he hasn't yet, „here, now we're bragging to you.“ The host declares the news an exclusive and congratulates him.

sections.subtitle: Kišni dan, Sveti Toma Mor i domino-efekt apostolata
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj pripovijeda kako je na Politeovu vjenčanju upoznao svoju suprugu
sections.content:
Voditelj ističe da su Politeo i Antonija jedan od brojnih parova koji su se upoznali moleći ispred bolnice. Govori o „koncentričnim krugovima“ i domino-efektu jer je i sam **na njihovu vjenčanju upoznao svoju buduću suprugu**.

Bio je to, prisjeća se, tmuran dan s jakom kišom i nije mu se dalo ići, „koliko god vas volim“, jer je mislio da tamo ionako poznaje sve. Ipak je došao i bio među prvima u crkvi. Njegova buduća supruga stigla je nekoliko sekundi kasnije. Počeli su razgovarati i nastavili se družiti u sali do kasno u noć. „Da ti nisi upoznao svoju suprugu, vjerojatno ne bih ni ja upoznao svoju“, kaže uz napomenu da se šali jer putove Gospodnje nitko ne zna.

U tome vidi kako Bog nagrađuje taj apostolat i kako mu je stalo do nerođene djece. Podsjeća na riječi koje Gospodin upućuje svojim svecima: „Ti se brini za moje, ja ću se brinuti za tvoje.“

Politeo se slaže i dodaje da je vjenčanje bilo **22. lipnja, na blagdan svetog Tome Mora**, kojega naziva zaštitnikom braka. Jutarnji pljusak kasnije je prestao i vrijeme je postalo lijepo. „Stvarno se spojilo nebo i zemlja“, zaključuje.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak uglavnom je usklađen s katoličkom vjerom u Božju providnost te prikazuje apostolat za zaštitu nerođenih i život obitelji kao dobra. Ipak, osobni susret nakon služenja ne treba predstavljati kao dokaz da Bog vjernost nužno nagrađuje željenim zemaljskim ishodom.
concerns: Izraz „Bog nagrađuje taj apostolat” i poslovica „Ti se brini za moje, ja ću se brinuti za tvoje” mogu se shvatiti kao obećanje uzvratne zemaljske nagrade; katoličko povjerenje u providnost ne znači da će služenje zajamčeno donijeti određenu osobnu korist.

Tvrdnja da je sveti Toma More zaštitnik braka nije potkrijepljena priloženim papinskim dokumentom: on ga proglašava zaštitnikom upravitelja i političara, premda istodobno ističe njegov život supruga i oca te njegovu brigu za obitelj.
magisterium.enrichment: Isusov poziv da se najprije traži Božje kraljevstvo uči pouzdanju u Oca, ali ne obećava da će se providnost uvijek očitovati kroz brak, uspjeh ili druge željene ishode. Susret na vjenčanju može se zato primiti kao osobno iskustvo zahvalnosti i providnosti, a ne kao opće pravilo o nagradi za apostolat. Sveti Toma More može nadahnuti vjernike i kao muž i otac, dok je njegov službeno navedeni patronat vezan uz upravitelje i političare.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with the Catholic faith in God's providence and presents the apostolate for the protection of the unborn and family life as goods. However, a personal meeting following service should not be presented as proof that God necessarily rewards faithfulness with a desired earthly outcome.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Jesus' call to seek first the Kingdom of God teaches trust in the Father, but does not promise that providence will always manifest through marriage, success, or other desired outcomes. The meeting at the wedding can therefore be received as a personal experience of gratitude and providence, and not as a general rule regarding a reward for an apostolate. Saint Thomas More can inspire the faithful also as a husband and father, while his officially stated patronage is associated with statesmen and politicians.
concerns_en: The phrase "God rewards that apostolate" and the saying "You take care of what is mine, and I will take care of what is yours" can be understood as a promise of a reciprocal earthly reward; Catholic trust in providence does not mean that service is guaranteed to bring a specific personal benefit.

The claim that Saint Thomas More is the patron saint of marriage is not substantiated by the attached papal document: it proclaims him patron saint of statesmen and politicians, although at the same time emphasizing his life as a husband and father and his care for his family.

sections.subtitle_en: A Rainy Day, Saint Thomas More, and the Domino Effect of the Apostolate
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host recounts how he met his wife at Politeo's wedding
sections.content_en:
The host points out that Politeo and Antonija are one of the many couples who met while praying in front of the hospital. He speaks of "concentric circles" and a domino effect because he himself **met his future wife at their wedding**.

It was, he recalls, a gloomy day with heavy rain and he did not feel like going, "as much as I love you," because he thought he already knew everyone there anyway. Yet he came and was among the first in the church. His future wife arrived a few seconds later. They started talking and continued hanging out in the hall until late at night. "If you hadn't met your wife, I probably wouldn't have met mine either," he says, noting that he is joking because no one knows the ways of the Lord.

In this, he sees how God rewards that apostolate and how much He cares about unborn children. He recalls the words that the Lord addresses to His saints: "You take care of what is mine, and I will take care of what is yours."

Politeo agrees and adds that the wedding was on **June 22, on the feast of Saint Thomas More**, whom he calls the patron saint of marriage. The morning downpour later stopped and the weather became beautiful. "Heaven and earth really came together," he concludes.

sections.subtitle: „Iscjeljenje očeva srca“: duhovne vježbe usmjerene na Boga Oca
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Politeo objašnjava strukturu programa „Iscjeljenje očeva srca“
sections.content:
Na voditeljevo pitanje od čega se program sastoji Politeo objašnjava da je **„Iscjeljenje očeva srca“** zapravo niz **duhovnih vježbi za muškarce**. Polaznik čita biblijske citate i odgovara na pitanja koja ih povezuju s njegovim životom. Tako upoznaje **Boga Oca**: tko je On, koliko nas ljubi i zašto smo stvoreni. Cilj je produbiti odnos s Ocem jer, kako kaže, „taj odnos liječi“.

Pred kraj programa slijedi **životna, odnosno velika ispovijed**. Polaznik dobiva opširnu pripremu, a svećenik mu je na raspolaganju i sat ili dva za razgovor, pitanja i cjelovitu ispovijed.

Politeo za sebe kaže da je samo „poslužitelj“, a da je središte programa polaznikov susret s Gospodinom.

magisterium.assessment: Opis je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkom duhovnošću: biblijsko razmatranje, produbljivanje odnosa s Bogom Ocem i raspoloživost za ispovijed mogu služiti obraćenju i rastu u Kristu. Izraz da odnos s Ocem „liječi“ prihvatljiv je kao duhovni opis, ali odlomak ne pojašnjava što se pod iscjeljenjem podrazumijeva.
concerns: Izraz „taj odnos liječi“ ne bi trebalo tumačiti kao obećanje automatskog ozdravljenja od psihičkih ili drugih zdravstvenih teškoća; iz odlomka nije jasno govori li se o duhovnom ozdravljenju, emocionalnoj potpori ili oboje.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveno shvaćene duhovne vježbe oslanjaju se na slušanje Božje riječi, molitvu i razlučivanje te usmjeravaju čovjeka prema obraćenju i nasljedovanju Krista. Ispovijed je sakrament pomirenja u kojem Božje milosrđe daruje oproštenje i potiče obnovljen život; stoga izraz „velika ispovijed“ valja razumjeti kao temeljitu pripravu za sakrament, a ne kao zaseban obred ili jamstvo da će sve životne rane odmah nestati.
