magisterium.assessment_en: The description is largely aligned with Catholic spirituality: biblical contemplation, deepening the relationship with God the Father, and availability for confession can serve conversion and growth in Christ. The expression that the relationship with the Father „heals“ is acceptable as a spiritual description, but the paragraph does not clarify what is meant by healing.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Spiritual exercises as understood by the Church rely on listening to the Word of God, prayer, and discernment, and direct man toward conversion and the following of Christ. Confession is the sacrament of reconciliation in which God's mercy bestows forgiveness and encourages a renewed life; therefore, the expression „major confession“ should be understood as thorough preparation for the sacrament, and not as a separate rite or a guarantee that all life's wounds will immediately disappear.
concerns_en: The expression „that relationship heals“ should not be interpreted as a promise of automatic healing from psychological or other health difficulties; from the paragraph it is not clear whether spiritual healing, emotional support, or both are being spoken of.

sections.subtitle_en: „Healing of the Father's Heart“: spiritual exercises focused on God the Father
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Politeo explains the structure of the program „Healing of the Father's Heart“
sections.content_en:
To the host's question of what the program consists of, Politeo explains that **„Healing of the Father's Heart“** is actually a series of **spiritual exercises for men**. The participant reads biblical quotes and answers questions that connect them with his life. In this way he gets to know **God the Father**: who He is, how much He loves us, and why we were created. The goal is to deepen the relationship with the Father because, as he says, „that relationship heals“.

Towards the end of the program follows a **life, that is, major confession**. The participant receives extensive preparation, and a priest is available to him even for an hour or two for conversation, questions, and a complete confession.

Politeo says of himself that he is only a „server“, and that the center of the program is the participant's encounter with the Lord.

sections.subtitle: Pet susreta za muškarce, tri dana šutnje za žene
sections.screenshot_description: Gost uspoređuje individualni format za muškarce i grupne seminare za žene
sections.content:
Program se provodi na dva načina:

- **Individualno (jedan na jedan):** pet susreta od sat i pol do dva sata. Na svakom susretu Politeo s polaznikom prođe i prodiskutira gradivo i preda mu materijale za sljedeći susret. Taj model primjenjuje kod muškaraca jer ih je zasad malo.
- **Grupno:** trodnevni seminari od petka do nedjelje, koji se zbog većeg broja polaznica održavaju za žene. Isti se sadržaj prolazi intenzivno, u samoći i šutnji, uz ispovijed i duhovni razgovor.

Između susreta polaznik kod kuće mora pronaći mir i vrijeme da pročita odlomke iz Svetog pisma i odgovori na pitanja. Kroz njih promišlja o odnosima u obitelji, o pobačaju i o zamjeranjima drugima i sebi. Cilj je, kaže Politeo, „dotaknuti svaku točku“ i iznijeti je pred Gospodina kako bi On mogao zaliječiti rane.

magisterium.assessment: Opis je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim pristupom obraćenju i duhovnoj pratnji: razmatranje Svetoga pisma, ispitivanje vlastitih odnosa i iznošenje rana pred Boga mogu poduprijeti iskreno kajanje i povjerenje u Božje milosrđe. Spominjanje ispovijedi dodatno je važno jer Crkva osobito upućuje osobe pogođene pobačajem na sakrament pomirenja i nadu u oproštenje, uz priznavanje stvarne težine učinjenoga.
concerns: Iz isječka nije jasno predstavlja li se „iscjeljenje” kao duhovni proces oslonjen na Božje milosrđe ili kao zajamčen ishod programa; katolički izvori podupiru nadu u oproštenje i pomoć pri oporavku, ali ne opravdavaju obećanje da će svaka emocionalna rana biti potpuno uklonjena.
Šutnja i osobno promišljanje mogu biti prikladni oblici duhovne vježbe, ali ne bi smjeli zamijeniti sakramentalnu ispovijed ni potrebnu stručnu pomoć kada osoba trpi ozbiljne psihološke teškoće.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički pristup drži zajedno dvije istine: pobačaj je teško moralno zlo, ali osoba koja ga je doživjela ili sudjelovala u njemu nije izvan dosega Božjega milosrđa; papa Benedikt XVI. pritom ističe potrebu pastoralne potpore i obnove. Iskreno suočavanje s grijehom i ranom ne služi osuđivanju, nego otvara put kajanju, oproštenju i novom životu; psalam moli Boga za čisto srce, a Isusovo „Ni ja te ne osuđujem; idi i odsada više nemoj griješiti” povezuje milosrđe s pozivom na obraćenje.

magisterium.assessment_en: The description is largely in alignment with the Catholic approach to conversion and spiritual accompaniment: contemplating Sacred Scripture, examining one's own relationships, and bringing wounds before God can support sincere repentance and trust in God's mercy. Mentioning confession is additionally important because the Church especially directs persons affected by abortion to the sacrament of reconciliation and the hope of forgiveness, while acknowledging the real gravity of what was done.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic approach holds together two truths: abortion is a grave moral evil, but a person who has experienced it or participated in it is not beyond the reach of God's mercy; Pope Benedict XVI thereby emphasizes the need for pastoral support and renewal. Sincere confrontation with sin and wound does not serve condemnation, but rather opens the way to repentance, forgiveness, and new life; the psalm prays to God for a clean heart, and Jesus's "Neither do I condemn you; go, and from now on do not sin any more" connects mercy with the call to conversion.
concerns_en: From the excerpt it is not clear whether "healing" is presented as a spiritual process relying on God's mercy or as a guaranteed outcome of the program; Catholic sources support hope in forgiveness and help in recovery, but do not justify a promise that every emotional wound will be completely removed.

Silence and personal reflection can be suitable forms of spiritual exercise, but they should not replace sacramental confession or necessary professional help when a person suffers from serious psychological difficulties.

sections.subtitle_en: Five meetings for men, three days of silence for women
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest compares the individual format for men and group seminars for women
sections.content_en:
The program is implemented in two ways:

- **Individually (one-on-one):** five meetings lasting from an hour and a half to two hours. At each meeting Politeo goes over and discusses the material with the participant and hands over the materials for the next meeting. He applies that model with men because there are few of them so far.
- **In groups:** three-day seminars from Friday to Sunday, which are held for women due to the larger number of female participants. The same content is covered intensively, in solitude and silence, with confession and spiritual conversation.

Between meetings, the participant must find peace and time at home to read passages from Sacred Scripture and answer questions. Through them, he or she reflects on family relationships, on abortion, and on resentments toward others and oneself. The goal, Politeo says, is "to touch every point" and bring it before the Lord so that He can heal the wounds.

sections.subtitle: I spontani i namjerni pobačaj ostavljaju ranu
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Politeo objašnjava zašto je program otvoren i za one koji su doživjeli spontani pobačaj
sections.content:
Voditelj pita zašto je program namijenjen i muškarcima koji su doživjeli spontani pobačaj, a ne samo onima koji su sudjelovali u namjernom.

Politeo odgovara da **obje vrste gubitka nose ranu**. Spontani pobačaj moguće je prihvatiti kao volju Božju, predati ga Gospodinu, znati da je dijete s Njim i imati zagovornika na nebu. Do toga, međutim, često vodi dug put, jer se i muškarci i žene znaju osuđivati. Kao primjere navodi misli poput „to nam je treće ili četvrto dijete, kako ćemo s autom“, zatim svađu sa suprugom ili sumnju da je presudio vlastiti „nedostatak ljubavi“. Tako čovjek završi u samoosuđivanju i neriješenom odnosu s Bogom.

Potrebno je, kaže, izmiriti se s Bogom i sa sobom te prihvatiti Boga Oca koji sve zna, a sebe kao čovjeka koji ne razumije sve, ali vjeruje Bogu. Cijelu sliku vidjet ćemo tek u nebu. Do tada treba vjerovati da Gospodin zna najbolje i da nije protiv nas. Ako netko osjeća krivnju, savjetuje ispovijed i razgovor sa suprugom. Prošlost se, ponavlja, ne može promijeniti, „možeš jedino ići naprijed“.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naglaskom na povjerenju u Boga, nadi i duhovnom pomirenju, a korisno prepoznaje da roditelji nakon gubitka mogu proživljavati bol i neutemeljenu samooptužbu. Ipak, tvrdnje da je spontani pobačaj jednostavno „volja Božja” i da je dijete sigurno s Bogom izrečene su previše kategorično: primjerenije je govoriti o nadi u Božje milosrđe i razlikovati Božje dopuštanje zla od njegova pozitivnog htijenja.
concerns: Formulacija „prihvatiti kao volju Božju” može sugerirati da Bog izravno želi smrt djeteta ili da je gubitak nešto što roditelji moraju bez pitanja pripisati njegovu planu; potrebno je razlikovati Božju providnost i dopuštanje patnje od tvrdnje da Bog pozitivno hoće svako zlo.
Tvrdnja da je dijete „s Njim” izražava kršćansku nadu, ali dostupni teološki tekst govori o nadi u spasenje umrle djece, a ne o sigurnoj spoznaji njihova konačnog stanja.

Treba jasnije reći da spontani pobačaj sam po sebi nije grijeh roditelja. Ispovijed može biti prikladna ako postoji stvarna krivnja zbog nekog grijeha, ali ne bi smjela poticati roditelje da se ispovijedaju zbog samog gubitka ili neutemeljenih osjećaja krivnje.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički teološki tekst o djeci koja umru bez krštenja ističe Božju spasenjsku volju i poziva kršćane da se za njih nadaju Božjem milosrđu, uz svijest da njihova sudbina nije izravno objavljena kao sigurna činjenica. Zato roditeljima može biti utješno povjeriti dijete Bogu i moliti za njega, bez predstavljanja te nade kao dogmatske sigurnosti. Razgovor sa supružnikom, pastoralna pratnja i sakrament pomirenja mogu pomoći u liječenju duhovne rane; ali potrebno je razlikovati potrebu za utjehom od stvarne moralne krivnje, a milosrđe i oproštenje posebno su važni kada je osoba doista sudjelovala u pobačaju.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with the Catholic emphasis on trust in God, hope, and spiritual reconciliation, and it usefully recognizes that parents after a loss can experience pain and unfounded self-accusation. Nevertheless, the claims that a spontaneous abortion is simply the "will of God" and that the child is certainly with God are stated too categorically: it is more appropriate to speak of hope in God's mercy and to distinguish God's permission of evil from His positive willing.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic theological text on infants who die without baptism highlights God's salvific will and calls Christians to hope in God's mercy for them, with the awareness that their fate is not directly revealed as a certain fact. Therefore, it can be comforting for parents to entrust the child to God and pray for him, without presenting that hope as dogmatic certainty. A conversation with the spouse, pastoral accompaniment, and the sacrament of reconciliation can help heal the spiritual wound; but it is necessary to distinguish the need for comfort from actual moral guilt, and mercy and forgiveness are especially important when a person has indeed participated in an abortion.
concerns_en: The formulation "to accept as the will of God" can suggest that God directly wills the death of the child or that the loss is something parents must unquestioningly attribute to His plan; it is necessary to distinguish God's providence and permission of suffering from the claim that God positively wills every evil.

The claim that the child is "with Him" expresses Christian hope, but the available theological text speaks of hope for the salvation of deceased infants, not of certain knowledge of their final state.

It should be stated more clearly that a spontaneous abortion in itself is not a sin of the parents. Confession may be appropriate if there is actual guilt due to some sin, but it should not encourage parents to confess because of the loss itself or unfounded feelings of guilt.

sections.subtitle_en: Both spontaneous and induced abortion leave a wound
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Politeo explains why the program is open also to those who have experienced a spontaneous abortion
sections.content_en:
The host asks why the program is intended also for men who have experienced a spontaneous abortion, and not only for those who participated in an induced one.

Politeo replies that **both types of loss carry a wound**. It is possible to accept a spontaneous abortion as the will of God, surrender it to the Lord, know that the child is with Him, and have an intercessor in heaven. To that, however, often leads a long path, because both men and women tend to judge themselves. As examples he cites thoughts like "this is our third or fourth child, how will we manage with the car", then an argument with the wife or a suspicion that one's own "lack of love" was the deciding factor. Thus a person ends up in self-condemnation and an unresolved relationship with God.

It is necessary, he says, to reconcile with God and with oneself and to accept God the Father who knows everything, and oneself as a human being who does not understand everything, but trusts in God. We will see the whole picture only in heaven. Until then, one should trust that the Lord knows best and that He is not against us. If someone feels guilt, he advises confession and a conversation with the wife. The past, he repeats, cannot be changed, "you can only move forward".

sections.subtitle: „Ja ću to sam riješiti“: zašto muškarci šute
sections.screenshot_description: Gost analizira razloge zbog kojih se muškarci rjeđe javljaju na program
sections.content:
Na pitanje zašto se muškarci javljaju rjeđe od žena Politeo navodi nekoliko razloga:

- **Muška samostalnost.** Problem nije u tome da muškarci ne osjećaju odgovornost, nego u stavu „ja mogu sam to riješiti, ne treba meni pomoć“. Žene su, kaže, spremnije potražiti pomoć, makar samo nekoga tko će ih voditi kroz proces.
- **Slaba vidljivost programa.** Informacija o programu u medijima je „dosta sakrivena“ i treba je tražiti, pa se glas širi polako, od usta do usta.
- **Šutnja u muškom društvu.** Muškarci rijetko jedni drugima govore da ih muči pobačaj, jer bi odgovor mogla biti zafrkancija. Zato to potiskuju ili ne rješavaju kako bi trebalo.

Ipak, muškarci se javljaju i Politeo vjeruje da će ih zbog dobrih rezultata i preporuka biti sve više. Naglašava da nije svakome nakon pobačaja nužan program. Neki se, poput njega, s Bogom izmire već u ispovijedi. „Ali ako osjećaš nemir, potraži pomoć. Tu smo, može se to riješiti.“

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom jer potiče muškarce koji pate nakon pobačaja da ne ostanu sami, nego potraže pomoć, te prepoznaje ispovijed kao put pomirenja s Bogom. Izraz „može se to riješiti” najbolje je razumjeti kao ohrabrenje, a ne kao jamstvo da će svaka emocionalna rana potpuno ili brzo nestati.
concerns: Opis muške šutnje i veće spremnosti žena da zatraže pomoć široka je generalizacija; ne treba je smatrati pravilom koje vrijedi za svakog muškarca ili ženu.
Ohrabrenje da se posljedice mogu „riješiti” može zvučati kao obećanje potpunog oporavka, iako oporavak može biti dugotrajan i različit za svaku osobu.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva prepoznaje da pobačaj može ostaviti duboke rane ne samo u ženama nego i u ljudima oko njih te cijeni pastoralne i druge oblike podrške za pomirenje i oporavak. Isusovo traženje izgubljenoga i radost zbog obraćenja (Lk 15,4–7) osvjetljuju zašto traženje pomoći nije slabost, nego može biti korak prema ozdravljenju i Božjem milosrđu. Ispovijed naviješta oproštenje i mir, dok duhovna pratnja ili druga primjerena pomoć mogu biti dodatna potpora; ne treba ih poistovjećivati sa sakramentom niti obećavati jednake rezultate svima.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching because it encourages men who suffer after an abortion not to remain alone, but to seek help, and recognizes confession as the path of reconciliation with God. The phrase “this can be resolved” is best understood as encouragement, and not as a guarantee that every emotional wound will disappear completely or quickly.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church recognizes that abortion can leave deep wounds not only in women but also in the people around them, and values pastoral and other forms of support for reconciliation and recovery. Jesus' search for the lost and joy over conversion (Lk 15:4–7) illuminate why seeking help is not a weakness, but can be a step toward healing and God's mercy. Confession proclaims forgiveness and peace, while spiritual direction or other appropriate help can be additional support; they should not be equated with the sacrament nor should equal results be promised to everyone.
concerns_en: The description of male silence and women's greater readiness to seek help is a broad generalization; it should not be considered a rule that applies to every man or woman.
The encouragement that the consequences can be “resolved” can sound like a promise of complete recovery, although recovery can be long-lasting and different for each person.

sections.subtitle_en: “I will solve this myself”: why men remain silent
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest analyzes the reasons why men reach out to the program less frequently
sections.content_en:
To the question of why men reach out less often than women, Politeo lists several reasons:

- **Male independence.** The problem is not that men do not feel responsibility, but in the attitude “I can solve this myself, I don't need help”. Women are, he says, more ready to seek help, even if only someone who will guide them through the process.
- **Low visibility of the program.** Information about the program in the media is “quite hidden” and one must search for it, so word spreads slowly, by word of mouth.
- **Silence in male company.** Men rarely tell each other that abortion is troubling them, because the response could be teasing. That is why they suppress it or do not resolve it as they should.

Still, men do reach out, and Politeo believes that due to good results and recommendations there will be more and more of them. He emphasizes that the program is not necessary for everyone after an abortion. Some, like him, are already reconciled with God in confession. “But if you feel restlessness, seek help. We are here, this can be resolved.”

sections.subtitle: Svjedočanstvo iz autobusa iz Međugorja
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj prepričava svjedočanstvo brata Stjepana s hodočašća u Međugorje
sections.content:
Voditelj se nada da će epizoda pomoći da se za program čuje među muškarcima. Napominje da žene nakon trodnevnog seminara budu „doista preobražene“ i vjeruje da tako biva i s muškarcima.

Zatim iznosi osobno svjedočanstvo. Vraćajući se s nedavnog **hodočašća u Međugorje**, pozvao je putnike u autobusu da podijele ono što im je na srcu. Javio se **brat Stjepan**, za kojega voditelj nije znao da je prošao program, iako je slutio da ga nešto muči. Dok je svjedočio, bio je „lagan kô perce“, a preobrazba se jasno vidjela. Oprostio je sebi nakon, kako voditelj procjenjuje, tridesetak i više godina od pobačaja.

Voditelj zahvaljuje Bogu na programu i žali što se njegova vrijednost toliko malo poznaje, jer je utemeljen na Svetom pismu i može osloboditi od grijeha prošlosti.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak na Bog može osloboditi čovjeka tereta prošlosti i preobraziti ga u skladu je s kršćanskom porukom obraćenja, oproštenja i nade. Ipak, izraz „oprostio je sebi” valja razumjeti kao prihvaćanje Božjeg oproštenja, a ne kao zamjenu za Božje oproštenje ili sakrament pomirenja.
concerns: Formulacija „oprostio je sebi” može ostaviti dojam da čovjek sam sebi dodjeljuje oproštenje; katolički je preciznije govoriti o kajanju i prihvaćanju Božjeg oproštenja, kojemu se vjernik, ako je potrebno, vraća i u sakramentu pomirenja.

Svjedočanstvo o vidljivoj preobrazbi i vrijednosti programa samo po sebi ne potvrđuje da program donosi isti ishod svima; dostupni opis ne daje dovoljno podataka za procjenu njegova konkretnog sadržaja.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička poruka o pobačaju istodobno čuva ozbiljnost moralnog zla i naviješta mogućnost oproštenja, mira i ozdravljenja; obraćenje uključuje iskreno suočavanje s prošlošću i povratak Bogu, a ne poricanje onoga što se dogodilo. Ivan Pavao II. izričito upućuje na Božje milosrđe i sakrament pomirenja, dok Novi zavjet povezuje obraćenje s oproštenjem grijeha (Dj 3,18–19).

citations.document_title: Abortion Shame, Abortion Shaming, and the Reintegrative Mercy of God (Evangelium Vitae §99)
To participants in the International Congress organized by the Pontifical John Paul II Institute for Studies on Marriage and Family (April 5, 2008)

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis that God can free man from the burden of the past and transform him is in accordance with the Christian message of conversion, forgiveness, and hope. However, the expression “he forgave himself” should be understood as the acceptance of God’s forgiveness, and not as a substitute for God’s forgiveness or the sacrament of reconciliation.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic message on abortion simultaneously preserves the gravity of moral evil and proclaims the possibility of forgiveness, peace, and healing; conversion includes an honest confrontation with the past and a return to God, not a denial of what happened. John Paul II explicitly points to God’s mercy and the sacrament of reconciliation, while the New Testament links conversion with the forgiveness of sins (Acts 3:18–19).
concerns_en: The phrasing “he forgave himself” can leave the impression that man grants forgiveness to himself; in Catholic terms it is more precise to speak of repentance and the acceptance of God’s forgiveness, to which the believer, if necessary, also returns in the sacrament of reconciliation.

The testimony about visible transformation and the value of the program does not in itself confirm that the program brings the same outcome to everyone; the available description does not provide enough data to assess its specific content.

sections.subtitle_en: Testimony from the bus from Međugorje
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host recounts the testimony of brother Stjepan from the pilgrimage to Međugorje
sections.content_en:
The host hopes that the episode will help the program be heard of among men. He notes that women after the three-day seminar are “truly transformed” and believes that it is so with men as well.

Then he shares a personal testimony. Returning from a recent **pilgrimage to Međugorje**, he invited the passengers on the bus to share what was on their hearts. **Brother Stjepan** spoke up, whom the host did not know had undergone the program, although he sensed that something was troubling him. While he was testifying, he was “light as a feather,” and the transformation was clearly visible. He forgave himself after, as the host estimates, some thirty or more years since the abortion.

The host thanks God for the program and regrets that its value is so little known, because it is rooted in Sacred Scripture and can liberate from the sins of the past.

sections.subtitle: „Ne mogu vjerovati, oprostio sam si“
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Politeo s emocijom opisuje polaznika koji na zadnjem susretu kaže da je oprostio sebi
sections.content:
Na pitanje što ga se u programu najviše dojmilo Politeo opisuje trenutak koji se ponavlja. Na četvrtom susretu iz razgovora često vidi da polaznik još nije oprostio sebi i nikad ne zna hoće li do toga doći. Gospodin ga, kaže, uvijek iznova iznenadi. Na posljednji susret polaznik dođe radostan i kaže: „Nevjerojatno, ne mogu vjerovati, oprostio sam si.“

Ističe da to nije njegova zasluga nego Božja i da ga upravo to fascinira. Svjestan je, objašnjava, da čovjek koji sebi ne oprosti ne može ići u nebo. Zato se uz polaznika i sam osjeća opterećeno, nada se i moli. Program najradije provodi tijekom kampanja, kada mnogi mole na te nakane, pa je sve „još natopljenije molitvom“.

Taj trenutak opisuje kao „živo čudo“: „Mrtav bješe i oživje.“ Pred sobom vidi novog, preobraženog čovjeka, brata u Kristu koji je uskrsnuo. „To te toliko napuni energijom, vjerom, snagom. Vidiš živoga Boga.“

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak snažno naglašava Božje milosrđe, obraćenje i mogućnost duhovnog ozdravljenja nakon pobačaja, što je u skladu s katoličkim naukom. Ipak, tvrdnja da čovjek koji sebi ne oprosti „ne može ići u nebo” teološki je neprecizna: može sugerirati da je psihološko samoopraštanje uvjet spasenja, dok katolički naglasak stavlja na Božji oprost, kajanje i pomirenje s Bogom.
concerns: Nije točno predstavljati samoopraštanje kao nužan uvjet ulaska u nebo. Osoba može žaliti zbog grijeha i iskreno se kajati te tražiti Božje milosrđe, a da joj je emocionalno prihvaćanje oproštenja još teško ili nedovršeno.

Oprost sebi može biti dio ljudskog i duhovnog ozdravljenja, ali nije isto što i Božje odrješenje niti zamjenjuje sakrament pomirenja. Bez tog razlikovanja izraz „oprostio sam si” može zamagliti tko oprašta grijehe i na čemu počiva nada spasenja.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva potvrđuje da pobačaj ostaje teško moralno zlo, ali istodobno poziva osobe koje su njime ranjene da se ne prepuste očaju, nego da se s pouzdanjem obrate Bogu i prime oproštenje i mir u sakramentu pomirenja. Izraz „Mrtav bješe i oživje” prikladno može opisivati obraćenje i obnovu, kao u prispodobi o izgubljenom sinu, ali je riječ o slici duhovnog povratka, a ne o tvrdnji da je osoba sama sebi podarila spasenje.

To participants in the International Congress organized by the Pontifical John Paul II Institute for Studies on Marriage and Family (April 5, 2008)
“What is Man?” (Ps 8:5). An itinerary of biblical anthropology

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage strongly emphasizes God's mercy, conversion, and the possibility of spiritual healing after abortion, which is in accordance with Catholic teaching. Nevertheless, the claim that a man who does not forgive himself "cannot go to heaven" is theologically imprecise: it may suggest that psychological self-forgiveness is a condition of salvation, whereas Catholic emphasis is placed on God's forgiveness, repentance, and reconciliation with God.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church affirms that abortion remains a grave moral evil, but at the same time calls persons who are wounded by it not to give in to despair, but with confidence to turn to God and receive forgiveness and peace in the sacrament of reconciliation. The expression "He was dead and came to life" can appropriately describe conversion and renewal, as in the parable of the prodigal son, but it is an image of spiritual return, not an assertion that the person granted salvation to themselves.
concerns_en: It is not accurate to present self-forgiveness as a necessary condition for entering heaven. A person can grieve over sin and sincerely repent and seek God's mercy, while the emotional acceptance of forgiveness is still difficult or incomplete for them.

Forgiving oneself can be part of human and spiritual healing, but it is not the same as God's absolution, nor does it replace the sacrament of reconciliation. Without this distinction, the expression "I forgave myself" can obscure who forgives sins and on what the hope of salvation rests.

sections.subtitle_en: "I can't believe it, I forgave myself"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Politeo with emotion describes a participant who at the last meeting says that he has forgiven himself
sections.content_en:
To the question of what impressed him the most in the program, Politeo describes a moment that recurs. At the fourth meeting, from the conversation he often sees that the participant has not yet forgiven himself and he never knows whether that will happen. The Lord, he says, always surprises him anew. To the last meeting, the participant comes joyful and says: "Incredible, I can't believe it, I forgave myself."

He emphasizes that this is not his merit but God's, and that this is precisely what fascinates him. He is aware, he explains, that a man who does not forgive himself cannot go to heaven. That is why, alongside the participant, he himself feels burdened, hopes, and prays. He prefers to run the program during campaigns, when many pray for these intentions, so everything is "even more soaked in prayer."

He describes that moment as a "living miracle": "He was dead and came to life." Before him he sees a new, transformed man, a brother in Christ who has risen. "That fills you with so much energy, faith, strength. You see the living God."

sections.subtitle: Straža svetog Josipa: muškarci na molitvi srijedom navečer
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje kako muškarci u Zagrebu srijedom mole Stražu svetog Josipa ispred bolnice
sections.content:
Voditelj primjećuje da oni koji sebi oproste postaju „veliki ratnici za život“. Posebno ga se dojmio prizor muškaraca koji mole ispred bolnica u sklopu **Straže svetog Josipa**. To je sat ili dva srijedom, kad tijekom kampanje ispred bolnica i domova zdravlja mole pretežno ili isključivo muškarci, njih pet, deset, petnaest ili dvadeset.

Politeo pojašnjava da u **Zagrebu** mole srijedom, na dan posvećen svetom Josipu, **od 21 do 22 sata**. U to vrijeme zaposleni mogu doći, a djeca su već u krevetu. Najčešće mole **Krunicu svetog Josipa, žalosti i radosti svetoga Josipa**, a u korizmi i **križni put za nerođene** te druge molitve. U Zagrebu zna doći i tridesetak muškaraca.

Navodi i primjer iz jedne kampanje. Kod bolnice **Sveti Duh** nisu mogli imati mjesto bdjenja, pa su dva ili tri puta obilazili bolnicu moleći krunicu na istu nakanu.

magisterium.assessment: Opis muške molitve, krunice i molitve za nerođene u skladu je s katoličkim poštovanjem ljudskog života od začeća te s kršćanskim svjedočenjem u njegovu obranu. Izraz da ljudi sebi oproste može biti duhovno neprecizan ako se shvati kao zamjena za Božje oproštenje i obraćenje.
concerns: Formulacija o samoopraštanju mogla bi se jasnije povezati s kajanjem, Božjim milosrđem i, kada je riječ o grijehu, sakramentom pomirenja; sama po sebi ipak ne dokazuje da se to naučava kao zamjena za Božje oproštenje.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva naučava da je ljudski život svet i nepovrediv od najranije faze te da poštovanje nerođenoga proizlazi iz biblijskog svjedočanstva o Božjoj brizi za čovjeka u majčinoj utrobi. Istodobno, pastoralni odgovor osobama ranjenima pobačajem treba sjediniti zaštitu života s milosrđem: pozivom na iskreno kajanje, Božjim oproštenjem u sakramentu pomirenja te duhovnom i ljudskom potporom.

citations.document_title: To participants in the Plenary Assembly of the Pontifical Academy for Life (February 26, 2011)

magisterium.assessment_en: The description of men's prayer, the Rosary, and prayer for the unborn is in accordance with Catholic respect for human life from conception and with Christian witness in its defense. The expression that people forgive themselves can be spiritually imprecise if understood as a substitute for God's forgiveness and conversion.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church teaches that human life is sacred and inviolable from the earliest stage and that respect for the unborn stems from biblical witness to God's care for man in the mother's womb. At the same time, the pastoral response to persons wounded by abortion should unite the protection of life with mercy: a call to sincere repentance, God's forgiveness in the sacrament of reconciliation, and spiritual and human support.
concerns_en: The formulation about self-forgiveness could be more clearly connected with repentance, God's mercy, and, when it comes to sin, the sacrament of reconciliation; in itself, however, it does not prove that this is taught as a substitute for God's forgiveness.

sections.subtitle_en: Saint Joseph's Watch: men at prayer on Wednesday evening
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes how men in Zagreb pray the Saint Joseph's Watch in front of the hospital on Wednesdays
sections.content_en:
The host notes that those who forgive themselves become "great warriors for life." He was particularly impressed by the sight of men praying in front of hospitals as part of **Saint Joseph's Watch**. That is an hour or two on Wednesdays, when during the campaign predominantly or exclusively men pray in front of hospitals and health centers, five, ten, fifteen, or twenty of them.

Politeo clarifies that in **Zagreb** they pray on Wednesdays, on the day dedicated to Saint Joseph, **from 9 to 10 PM**. At that time, employed people can come, and the children are already in bed. Most often they pray the **Rosary of Saint Joseph, the sorrows and joys of Saint Joseph**, and in Lent also the **Way of the Cross for the unborn** and other prayers. In Zagreb, even around thirty men can come.

He also cites an example from one campaign. Near the **Sveti Duh** hospital, they could not have a vigil site, so they walked around the hospital two or three times praying the Rosary for the same intention.
keywords_en: Way of the Cross for the unborn

sections.subtitle: Očinstvo između milosrđa i stege
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Politeo govori o najvećem izazovu očinstva
sections.content:
Voditelj podsjeća da je Politeo, s djetetom koje očekuje s Antonijom, otac petero djece, odnosno šestero ubraja li se i ranije pobačeno dijete. Pita ga koji su najveći izazovi očinstva.

Najtežim mu je, kaže, pronaći **ravnotežu između slike milosrdnog Boga Oca** koju želi prenijeti djeci i **oštrine** kojom „otac koji ljubi sina ga kudi“. Priznaje da možda previše razmišlja o tome kako bi se plodovi trebali vidjeti ranije, iako zna da tako ne ide. Svake večeri predaje Gospodinu sve što su on i supruga pogrešno učinili da On ublaži moguće rane. Ipak, smatra da im u cjelini ide dobro.

Očinstvo opisuje kao „radost i žalost u isto vrijeme“, dok fizički napor smatra normalnim, pa i blagoslovom. Djeca mu sve vraćaju radošću, a posebno ga raduju trenuci kad vidi da se nešto „ipak primilo“. Primjer je sin koji bratu objašnjava kako nešto treba napraviti, iako to sam ne radi: „Znači da je čuo i zapamtio, samo ne odrađuje.“ Voditelj dodaje da su djeca poput spužve, pa treba paziti što se pred njima govori.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: prikazuje očinstvo kao spoj ljubavi, milosrđa, odgovornog ispravljanja i strpljivosti prema postupnom sazrijevanju djece. Opis večernjeg povjeravanja vlastitih pogrešaka Gospodinu također odgovara kršćanskom pouzdanju u Božje milosrđe, premda je važno da se „oštrina” u odgoju ne shvati kao opravdanje za nasilje ili ponižavanje.
concerns: Izraz „oštrina” nije dodatno pojašnjen; ako bi označavao nasilno ili ponižavajuće kažnjavanje, takav bi pristup bio neprihvatljiv, no odlomak ne kaže da se to događa.
magisterium.enrichment: U Svetom pismu ukor može biti izraz ljubavi kad je usmjeren na dobro djeteta, kao u Izrekama 3,11–12, ali kršćanska stega mora ostati razborita i ljubavlju vođena. Papinska biblijska komisija izričito napominje da se nasilne odgojne prakse danas ne mogu prihvatiti, dok ispravljanje i primjerena disciplina ostaju dio odgovornog odgoja; roditeljski cilj jest pomoći djetetu da raste u slobodi i odgovornosti.

citations.document_title: “What is Man?” (Ps 8:5). An itinerary of biblical anthropology
General Audience of 2 March 2016: 9. Mercy and correction

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching: it presents fatherhood as a combination of love, mercy, responsible correction, and patience toward the gradual maturation of children. The description of entrusting one's own mistakes to the Lord every evening also corresponds to Christian trust in God's mercy, although it is important that "severity" in upbringing is not understood as a justification for violence or humiliation.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In Sacred Scripture, reproof can be an expression of love when it is directed toward the good of the child, as in Proverbs 3:11–12, but Christian discipline must remain prudent and guided by love. The Pontifical Biblical Commission explicitly notes that violent disciplinary practices cannot be accepted today, while correction and appropriate discipline remain part of responsible upbringing; the parental goal is to help the child grow in freedom and responsibility.
concerns_en: The term "severity" is not further clarified; if it were to denote violent or humiliating punishment, such an approach would be unacceptable, but the passage does not state that this is occurring.

sections.subtitle_en: Fatherhood between mercy and discipline
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Politeo speaks about the greatest challenge of fatherhood
sections.content_en:
The host recalls that Politeo, with the child he is expecting with Antonija, is a father of five children, or six if the previously miscarried child is also counted. He asks him what the greatest challenges of fatherhood are.

The hardest thing for him, he says, is to find **a balance between the image of the merciful God the Father** that he wants to convey to the children and the **severity** with which "a father who loves his son chastises him." He admits that he might think too much about how the fruits should be seen earlier, even though he knows it does not work that way. Every evening he surrenders to the Lord everything that he and his wife did wrong, so that He may soothe possible wounds. Still, he considers that on the whole they are doing well.

He describes fatherhood as "joy and sorrow at the same time," while he considers physical exertion normal, even a blessing. The children return everything to him with joy, and he is especially gladdened by the moments when he sees that something "took hold after all." An example is the son who explains to his brother how something should be done, even though he does not do it himself: "It means that he heard and remembered, he just isn't carrying it out." The host adds that children are like sponges, so one must be careful about what is said in front of them.

sections.subtitle: Večernji ritual: zahvale, Anđele čuvaru i krunica dok djeca tonu u san
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje večernju obiteljsku molitvu s djecom

magisterium.assessment: Opis je u visokoj mjeri usklađen s katoličkim naukom: obiteljska molitva, zahvaljivanje i zajednička krunica konkretno žive poziv obitelji da bude domaća Crkva i da djecu uvodi u molitvu primjerom. Posebno je dobro što roditelji uzimaju u obzir dob i pažnju djece te im molitvu ne nameću na način koji bi je pretvorio u puku prisilu.
concerns: Izraz da djeca „znaju da se krunica mora moliti” može zvučati kao obveza nametnuta bez razumijevanja, ali opis ne pokazuje da roditelji pribjegavaju prisili; njihova odluka da djecu ne tjeraju na sudjelovanje ublažava tu moguću nejasnoću.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva potiče roditelje da djecu uče molitvi ponajprije vlastitim primjerom, a obiteljsku molitvu smatra prirodnim uvodom u molitvu cijele Crkve. Krunica je osobito prikladna za zajedničku molitvu jer usmjerava obitelj prema otajstvima Kristova života uz Mariju; zahvaljivanje za konkretne događaje dana dodatno odgaja djecu da prepoznaju Božje darove. Sudjelovanje djece treba biti postupno i prilagođeno njihovoj dobi, u skladu s poštovanjem njihove slobode.

citations.document_title: General Audience of 26 August 2015: The family - 24. Prayer

magisterium.assessment_en: The description is highly aligned with Catholic teaching: family prayer, thanksgiving, and the communal Rosary concretely live out the family's calling to be a domestic Church and to introduce children to prayer by example. It is especially good that the parents take into account the age and attention span of the children and do not impose prayer on them in a way that would turn it into mere coercion.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church encourages parents to teach children to pray primarily by their own example, and considers family prayer a natural introduction to the prayer of the whole Church. The Rosary is especially suitable for communal prayer because it directs the family toward the mysteries of Christ's life alongside Mary; thanksgiving for concrete events of the day additionally educates children to recognize God's gifts. Children's participation should be gradual and adapted to their age, in accordance with respect for their freedom.
concerns_en: The expression that the children „know that the Rosary must be prayed” may sound like an obligation imposed without understanding, but the description does not show that the parents resort to coercion; their decision not to force the children to participate mitigates this potential ambiguity.

sections.subtitle: Svjedočiti životom, bez glume svetosti
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Politeo govori o autentičnom životu kao svjedočanstvu djeci
sections.content:
Voditelj ocjenjuje da roditelji Politeo postavljaju dobre temelje i da će djeca pamtiti zajedničke molitvene trenutke.

Politeo odgovara da se trude svjedočiti vlastitim životom, jer djeca ionako sve „pokupe“, i živjeti što autentičnije. „Ne treba tu glumit da smo sveci, nismo, ali trudimo se bit bolji.“

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom snažno usklađen s katoličkim shvaćanjem roditelja kao prvih odgojitelja u vjeri: naglašava svjedočenje vlastitim životom i iskreno nastojanje da se bude bolji, a ne glumljenje savršenstva. Važno je da autentičnost ne znači opravdavanje pogrešaka, nego nastojanje da život sve više bude u skladu s vjerom.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveni nauk ističe da djeca uče iz primjera roditelja i da su obiteljska molitva i svakodnevno svjedočanstvo važni za prenošenje vjere. Tako shvaćena autentičnost uključuje i dosljednost između vjere i života te ponizno prihvaćanje potrebe za rastom i obraćenjem.

citations.document_title: To the Bishops of the Episcopal Conference of France on their "ad Limina" visit (February 20, 2004)

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely strongly aligned with the Catholic understanding of parents as the first educators in the faith: it emphasizes witnessing through one's own life and a sincere effort to be better, rather than pretending perfection. It is important that authenticity does not mean justifying mistakes, but striving for life to be increasingly in accordance with the faith.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Church teaching emphasizes that children learn from the example of their parents and that family prayer and daily witness are important for the transmission of the faith. Authenticity understood in this way also includes consistency between faith and life and a humble acceptance of the need for growth and conversion.

sections.content_en:
The host assesses that the Politeo parents are laying good foundations and that the children will remember shared moments of prayer.

Politeo responds that they try to witness through their own lives, because children "pick up" everything anyway, and to live as authentically as possible. "There is no need to pretend to be saints here, we are not, but we try to be better."

sections.subtitle: Blic pitanja: od latinske poslovice do Antonije Politeo
sections.screenshot_description: Gost odgovara na blic pitanja „ili-ili“ i citira latinsku poslovicu
sections.content:
Pred kraj voditelj postavlja **blic pitanja „ili-ili“** i najavljuje da su neka provokativna, a neka komična.

- **Otac koji vodi u molitvi ili otac koji sluša?** Otac koji sluša. Politeo citira latinsku poslovicu, „jedinu koju znam“, kako sam kaže: *„Noli tu imperare antequam didiceris obedire“*, odnosno ne zapovijedaj dok ne naučiš slušati. Vođenje je u redu samo ako ide uz slušanje.
- **Ante Čaljkušić ili sveti Ante Padovanski?** Sveti Ante Padovanski. „Zna se“, dodaje voditelj.
- **Program u grupi ili individualni rad?** Zasad individualni, jer je na njemu vidio rezultate, a grupni program još nije vodio pa o njemu ne može suditi.
- **Antonija Šola ili Antonija Politeo?** Antonija Politeo.
- **Poruka nade ili apel na odgovornost?** Poruka nade, „uvijek nade“, jer nada „može čovjeka iz bezdana povući“.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim pogledom na roditeljsku odgovornost, jer ističe slušanje, strpljivo vodstvo i nadu, bez tvrdnji koje bi proturječile vjeri ili Svetom pismu. Izjava da nada može čovjeka izvući iz bezdana zvuči ohrabrujuće, ali sama po sebi ne pojašnjava da je kršćanska nada konačno ukorijenjena u Bogu.
concerns: Moguća je, ali ne i nužna, nejasnoća oko toga znači li „nada” prvenstveno ljudski optimizam ili kršćansku krepost koja se oslanja na Boga; u odlomku se to ne razrađuje.
magisterium.enrichment: Slušanje ne isključuje očev autoritet ni dužnost odgoja: biblijski prikaz roditeljske odgovornosti povezuje odgoj u Gospodinu s upozorenjem da se djecu ne razdražuje ili obeshrabruje. Kršćanska nada nije puko uvjerenje da će okolnosti nužno krenuti nabolje, nego pouzdanje u Boga i njegovu pomoć, čak i u teškim situacijama. Prednost individualnom radu može biti razborit osobni sud o vlastitom iskustvu, a ne tvrdnja da je individualni pristup aina paremjeran ili bolji za sve.

citations.document_title: “What is Man?” (Ps 8:5). An itinerary of biblical anthropology
General Audience of 26 January 2022 - Catechesis on Saint Joseph: 9. Saint Joseph, a man who "dreams"

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with the Catholic view on parental responsibility, as it emphasizes listening, patient leadership, and hope, without claims that would contradict the faith or Sacred Scripture. The statement that hope can pull a man out of the abyss sounds encouraging, but in itself does not clarify that Christian hope is ultimately rooted in God.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Listening does not exclude a father's authority nor the duty of upbringing: the biblical presentation of parental responsibility links upbringing in the Lord with an admonition not to provoke or discourage children. Christian hope is not mere conviction that circumstances will necessarily turn for the better, but trust in God and His help, even in difficult situations. Preference for individual work can be a prudent personal judgment about one's own experience, and not a claim that the individual approach is universally superior or better for everyone.
concerns_en: Ambiguity is possible, though not necessary, regarding whether "hope" means primarily human optimism or a Christian virtue that relies on God; in the passage, this is not elaborated.

sections.subtitle_en: Quickfire questions: from a Latin proverb to Antonija Politeo
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest answers "either-or" quickfire questions and quotes a Latin proverb
sections.content_en:
Towards the end, the host asks **"either-or" quickfire questions** and announces that some are provocative and some comical.

- **A father who leads in prayer or a father who listens?** A father who listens. Politeo quotes a Latin proverb, "the only one I know," as he says himself: *"Noli tu imperare antequam didiceris obedire"*, that is, do not command until you have learned to obey/listen. Leading is fine only if it goes along with listening.
- **Ante Čaljkušić or Saint Anthony of Padua?** Saint Anthony of Padua. "It is known," adds the host.
- **Group program or individual work?** For now individual, because he has seen results from it, and he has not yet led a group program so he cannot judge it.
- **Antonija Šola or Antonija Politeo?** Antonija Politeo.
- **A message of hope or an appeal to responsibility?** A message of hope, "always hope," because hope "can pull a man out of the abyss."

sections.subtitle: „Nisi sam. Može biti bolje.“
sections.screenshot_description: Vedran Politeo upućuje poruku nade muškarcima koji se bore s posljedicama pobačaja
sections.content:
Za kraj voditelj traži poruku muškarcima koji su doživjeli namjerni ili spontani pobačaj, bore se s tim i možda dvoje trebaju li se javiti na program.

Politeo odgovara kratko: **„Nisi sam. Nisi sam i može biti bolje.“** Svima koji su prošli program, kaže, bolje je nego prije, nijedan nije zažalio i svi su pronašli mir. „Koliko god sad izgleda da nema sutra, da ne može biti bolje i da si sve probao, to nije istina. Može biti bolje, i ja sam živi svjedok toga.“

magisterium.assessment: Poruka „Nisi sam” i poticaj na nadu u skladu su s kršćanskim navještajem Božjeg milosrđa te s crkvenim pozivom na pastoralnu i duhovnu potporu osobama ranjenima iskustvom pobačaja. Ipak, tvrdnja da je svim polaznicima programa bolje i da nitko nije požalio treba ostati prikazana kao osobno svjedočanstvo, a ne kao jamstvo da će svatko doživjeti isti ishod.
concerns: Apsolutna tvrdnja o iskustvu svih polaznika može stvoriti nerealno očekivanje brzog ili jednakog oporavka; iscjeljenje može biti osobno i postupno.
Namjerni pobačaj i spontani pobačaj nisu moralno istovjetni: spontani gubitak trudnoće ne treba prikazivati kao osobnu krivnju, premda i on može izazvati duboku žalost.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva istodobno naziva namjerni pobačaj teškom nepravdom i poziva da se prema ranjenim osobama pristupa s milosrđem, delikatnošću i nadom u oproštenje i obnovu. Benedikt XVI. izričito cijeni pastoralne inicijative za pomirenje i liječenje osoba pogođenih dramom pobačaja, dok crkveni nauk usmjerava na sakrament pomirenja one koji traže oproštenje.

citations.document_title: To participants in the International Congress organized by the Pontifical John Paul II Institute for Studies on Marriage and Family (April 5, 2008)

magisterium.assessment_en: The message "You are not alone" and the encouragement toward hope are in accordance with the Christian proclamation of God's mercy and with the Church's call for pastoral and spiritual support for persons wounded by the experience of abortion. Nevertheless, the claim that all participants of the program are better off and that no one regretted it should remain presented as a personal testimony, and not as a guarantee that everyone will experience the same outcome.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church simultaneously calls induced abortion a grave injustice and calls for approaching wounded persons with mercy, delicacy, and hope in forgiveness and renewal. Benedict XVI explicitly values pastoral initiatives for reconciliation and healing of persons affected by the drama of abortion, while Church teaching directs toward the sacrament of reconciliation those who seek forgiveness.
concerns_en: An absolute claim regarding the experience of all participants can create an unrealistic expectation of rapid or equal recovery; healing can be personal and gradual.
Induced abortion and spontaneous abortion are not morally equivalent: spontaneous pregnancy loss should not be presented as personal guilt, even though it can also cause profound grief.

sections.subtitle_en: "You are not alone. It can get better."
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vedran Politeo addresses a message of hope to men struggling with the consequences of abortion
sections.content_en:
To conclude, the host asks for a message for men who have experienced induced or spontaneous abortion, are struggling with it and are perhaps hesitating whether they should reach out to the program.

Politeo answers briefly: **"You are not alone. You are not alone and it can get better."** Everyone who went through the program, he says, is better off than before, not one has regretted it and all have found peace. "No matter how much it seems right now that there is no tomorrow, that it cannot get better and that you have tried everything, that is not true. It can get better, and I am a living witness to that."

sections.subtitle: Zahvala, odjava i najava epizode o novcu u crkvi
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj zahvaljuje gostu i najavljuje sljedeću epizodu
sections.content:
Voditelj ocjenjuje da je to najbolja moguća završna poruka. Zahvaljuje Vedranu na gostovanju i izražava uvjerenje da je „mnogima progovorio“. Politeo zahvaljuje na pozivu i kaže da se rado odazvao.

Voditelj najavljuje sljedeću „Redefiniciju“ za idući mjesec i poziva gledatelje da se pridruže na **Patreon** profilu, gdje se nova epizoda može pogledati odmah.

U kratkom isječku iz sljedeće epizode neidentificirani sugovornik otvara temu **novca u crkvi i darivanja**. Primjećuje da novac u crkvi „uvijek ima puno veću težinu nego u birtiji“: sto kuna za rundu nikome nije problem, a dvadeset kuna u crkvi doživljava se kao velik dar.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak ne iznosi izričit nauk o darivanju niti proturječi katoličkom nauku; usporedba samo opaža da ljudi često drukčije doživljavaju trošenje novca za crkvu i za razonodu. Poziv na Patreon i najava teme sami po sebi ne daju dovoljno osnove za prosudbu o načinu prikupljanja ili uporabi novca.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk potiče vjernike da prema svojim mogućnostima podupiru potrebe Crkve, njezino poslanje i djela ljubavi, ali darivanje treba biti slobodno i velikodušno, a ne iznuđeno. Istodobno se sakramentalni život ne smije komercijalizirati niti prikazivati kao usluga s cjenikom; odgovornost vjernika za potrebe zajednice ne znači da se sakramenti naplaćuju.

citations.document_title: Instruction "The pastoral conversion of the Parish community in the service of the evangelising mission of the Church", of the Congregation for the Clergy, 20.07.2020

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage does not present an explicit teaching on giving, nor does it contradict Catholic teaching; the comparison merely observes that people often perceive spending money on the church and on leisure differently. The call to Patreon and the announcement of the topic do not in themselves provide sufficient basis for judgment regarding the manner of collecting or the use of money.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching encourages the faithful to support the needs of the Church, her mission, and works of charity according to their means, but giving should be free and generous, not coerced. At the same time, sacramental life must not be commercialized nor presented as a service with a price list; the responsibility of the faithful for the needs of the community does not mean that sacraments are charged for.

sections.subtitle_en: Thanks, sign-off, and announcement of the episode on money in the church
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host thanks the guest and announces the next episode
sections.content_en:
The host assesses that this is the best possible closing message. He thanks Vedran for being a guest and expresses conviction that he has „spoken to many“. Politeo thanks him for the invitation and says that he gladly responded.

The host announces the next „Redefinicija“ for the following month and invites viewers to join on the **Patreon** profile, where the new episode can be watched immediately.

In a short clip from the next episode, an unidentified interlocutor opens the topic of **money in the church and giving**. He notes that money in the church „always carries much more weight than in a pub“: a hundred kunas for a round is no problem for anyone, while twenty kunas in church is perceived as a big gift.
